seoul-001.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
seoul-001.summary: Seoul's foremost royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty, renowned for its grand scale and beautiful architecture
seoul-001.historicalDescription: Built in 1395 (the 4th year of King Taejo's reign), Gyeongbokgung Palace served as the main palace of the Joseon Dynasty for 500 years. Though it housed the Japanese Government-General building during the colonial period, post-liberation restoration efforts have steadily returned it to its original form. Major structures include Geunjeongjeon, Gyeonghoeru, and Jagyeongjeon, and the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony takes place daily.
seoul-001.emotionalDescription: Passing through Gwanghwamun Gate, you are immediately awed by the magnificent scale of Gyeongbokgung. Walking alongside the reflections on Gyeonghoeru Pond transports you to feeling like royalty of the Joseon era. Especially during autumn foliage, snowy winter evenings, or late-night openings linked with Changdeokgung, the atmosphere is truly magical.
seoul-001.bestTime: Spring (cherry blossoms), Autumn (fall foliage), Night opening

seoul-002.name: Changdeokgung Palace
seoul-002.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Joseon palace, celebrated for the stunning natural scenery of its Secret Garden (Biwon)
seoul-002.historicalDescription: Changdeokgung was built in 1405 during the reign of King Taejong as an auxiliary palace to Gyeongbokgung. Well-preserved even through the Japanese colonial period, it was later inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its rear garden (Biwon) showcases the pinnacle of Joseon garden design, seeking harmony with nature rather than artificial landscaping — a place where kings rested and honed their civil and martial skills.
seoul-002.emotionalDescription: Walking through Changdeokgung's rear garden (Biwon) is a journey into the essence of traditional Korean garden art. Along naturally formed paths following the valley, you breathe in the scent of the forest and hear crystal-clear water, empathizing with the tranquility felt by kings. The harmony of crimson maple leaves and blue moss in autumn is truly breathtaking.
seoul-002.bestTime: Spring, Autumn (foliage season), Huwon tour essential

seoul-003.name: Deoksugung Palace
seoul-003.summary: A unique palace where Western-style architecture coexists with traditional Korean buildings, site of the Korean Empire proclamation
seoul-003.historicalDescription: Deoksugung, originally called Gyeongun Palace, began as a refuge for King Seonjo during the Imjin War. In 1897, Emperor Gojong moved here from the Russian legation and proclaimed the Korean Empire, elevating it to an imperial palace. It uniquely combines traditional Korean buildings with Western-style structures such as Seokjojeon and Jeonggwanheon, reflecting the changing times.
seoul-003.emotionalDescription: Deoksugung emanates a special atmosphere, as if standing at the boundary between tradition and modernity. Walking along the stone-walled path, you sense the transition from Joseon to the Korean Empire, and the view of elegant traditional curves harmonizing with the modern Seokjojeon is a visceral experience of history's flow. The palace illuminated at night during late openings is simply fantastic.

seoul-004.name: Gyeonghuigung Palace
seoul-004.summary: A restored secondary Joseon palace of considerable scale, a historic space connected to Seoul's City Wall
seoul-004.historicalDescription: Gyeonghuigung was built in 1617 as a secondary palace. Renamed during the reign of King Sunjong, it was an important palace where later Joseon kings resided. Currently, Heunghwamun Gate, Sungjeongjeon, and Honghwamun have been restored and, connected to Changuimun, form part of the Seoul City Wall walking trail.
seoul-004.emotionalDescription: Gyeonghuigung is quieter than other major palaces, allowing you to leisurely sense its history. Walking among the restored buildings, you can imagine the atmosphere of a late Joseon palace, and the blend of the northern mountain scenery creates a sense of peace. It is a great spot to combine a historical stroll with the Seoul City Wall trail.

seoul-005.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
seoul-005.summary: A palace that served as an emotional retreat for Joseon kings, an urban oasis where a greenhouse and gardens blend
seoul-005.historicalDescription: Changgyeonggung was built in 1418 by King Sejong for the Queen Mother. Originally an auxiliary palace of Changdeokgung, a bridge was built connecting the two palaces during King Seongjong's reign. During the Japanese colonial period it was reduced to a zoo and botanical garden, but restoration from the 1980s gave it its current form. Key structures include Myeongjeongjeon, Honghwamun, and the Great Greenhouse.
seoul-005.emotionalDescription: Unlike other palaces, Changgyeonggung has a more familiar and relaxed atmosphere. The contrast of the glass Great Greenhouse with traditional wooden architecture, and strolling around Gyeongchunjeon with its grand fountain, brings a peaceful feeling. Walking among spring cherry blossoms and bamboo groves is particularly memorable.

seoul-006.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
seoul-006.summary: A traditional hanok-dense neighborhood preserving 600 years of history, once the residential area of Joseon nobility
seoul-006.historicalDescription: Bukchon, meaning 'northern village,' was located to the north between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung Palaces during the Joseon Dynasty. Maintained as the residence of nobles and royalty, it remains a treasure trove of traditional hanok houses. A significant number were preserved through modernization, and today around 900 hanok remain, making it Seoul's leading traditional culture space.
seoul-006.emotionalDescription: Walking through Bukchon's alleyways feels like traveling through time. The curved beauty of tiled roofs, stone walls, and each wooden nameplate speaks of Korean traditional architectural craftsmanship. Quietly wandering the lanes while imagining Joseon noble life, the hushed ancient atmosphere of the city overwhelms you. Bukchon at sunset is even more beautiful.

seoul-007.name: Namsangol Hanok Village
seoul-007.summary: A traditional hanok complex on the slopes of Namsan, a cultural space for folk experiences and performances
seoul-007.historicalDescription: Namsangol Hanok Village was established in 1998 on the slopes of Namsan. Five traditional hanok buildings from across Seoul were relocated and restored here, showcasing the lifestyle of middle and lower-class Joseon citizens. Various cultural experiences are available, including traditional wedding ceremonies, folk games, and traditional performances. The oldest hanok, Kim Chunyeong's house, was built in 1860.
seoul-007.emotionalDescription: This hanok village nestled beneath N Seoul Tower is a traditional retreat within the bustling city. In the hanok complex blending with Namsan's nature, you can sip traditional tea or experience folk games to connect with the lives of ancestors. The harmony of the autumn foliage of Namsan with the hanok makes for beautiful photographs.

seoul-008.name: Insadong
seoul-008.summary: A traditional culture street lined with antiques, folk crafts, and traditional teahouses — an artistic quarter
seoul-008.historicalDescription: Insadong was historically a government district in the Joseon era and transformed into an antique street in modern times. Antique shops began gathering here from the 1930s, and during the colonial period it was also a place where cultural artifacts were traded. Today it is a representative traditional culture street featuring crafts, paintings, calligraphy, folk goods, and traditional teahouses.
seoul-008.emotionalDescription: Insadong's narrow alleyways carry the most distinctly Korean atmosphere in Seoul. Lingering in antique shops listening to the stories of old objects, and drinking traditional tea in a hanok teahouse, is a special time connecting the present with the past. The weekend scene on Insadong Street is a vibrant snapshot of living traditional culture.

seoul-009.name: National Museum of Korea
seoul-009.summary: Korea's largest museum, a treasury of history and culture housing over 220,000 artifacts
seoul-009.historicalDescription: The National Museum of Korea opened in 1945 and relocated to Yongsan in 2005. It houses over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history and culture from prehistoric times to the modern era. Highlights include national treasures like the Gilt-Bronze Maitreya in Meditation and the Geumgwanchong Gold Crown, alongside 6 permanent exhibition halls and a special exhibition gallery.
seoul-009.emotionalDescription: Visiting the National Museum of Korea is a journey through Korean history. Encountering thousands of years of culture — from prehistoric pottery to Joseon white porcelain — within the grand building and spacious halls, you feel a simultaneous sense of awe and pride for your people's history. The lake in front of the museum provides one of Seoul's hidden night views.

seoul-010.name: National Folk Museum of Korea
seoul-010.summary: A museum showcasing Korea's traditional folk life history, located within Gyeongbokgung Palace
seoul-010.historicalDescription: The National Folk Museum of Korea opened in 1945 and moved to the Heungnyemun district of Gyeongbokgung in 1993. It is the nation's largest folk museum, systematically preserving and displaying the life history and folk culture of the Korean people. Through over 10,000 artifacts, you can explore ancestors' daily lives, rituals, and folk beliefs, with life-size folk village displays as a highlight.
seoul-010.emotionalDescription: The National Folk Museum is a place where you can feel the wisdom and care of our ancestors. Viewing various household items, ritual objects, and traditional clothing deepens your understanding of Korean life history, and strolling through reconstructed traditional homes brings empathy for the daily lives of the past. It is particularly a wonderful educational space to visit with children.

seoul-011.name: Seoul Forest
seoul-011.summary: A large urban park combining a natural ecology zone and a culture and arts park
seoul-011.historicalDescription: Seoul Forest was established in 2005 as Seoul's premier urban park. This site was a royal hunting ground in the Joseon era, used as a horse racing track during the colonial period, and operated as a golf course and amusement park in the 1970s–80s before being transformed into a public park. Spanning 1.2 million m², it includes a natural ecology forest, a culture and arts park, and an experiential learning area.
seoul-011.emotionalDescription: Seoul Forest is a natural refuge within the city. Seasonal landscapes — spring cherry blossoms, lush summer trees, autumn silver grass, winter snow — invite communion with nature and healing. Walking along the riverside path connected to the Han River, you can feel tranquility in the harmony of city and nature.

seoul-012.name: Yeouido Park
seoul-012.summary: A large park at the heart of Yeouido, famous as a prime cherry blossom viewing spot
seoul-012.historicalDescription: Yeouido Park was established in 1999 as an urban park. The site hosted an international airport until the 1970s, then served as an illegal parking lot before being developed into a public park. Covering approximately 230,000 m², it is managed by the Han River Business Office. Famous for its spring cherry blossom festival, it is adjacent to the National Assembly and the Han River.
seoul-012.emotionalDescription: Spring in Yeouido Park is one of Seoul's most beautiful sights. Walking under the cherry blossom tunnel while petals drift down is breathtaking, and the cherry blossom scenery with the Han River as a backdrop offers urban romance. Beyond cherry blossom season, the wide lawn provides a relaxing retreat.

seoul-013.name: N Seoul Tower
seoul-013.summary: Seoul's iconic landmark atop Namsan, famous for its observatory and night views
seoul-013.historicalDescription: N Seoul Tower was built in 1969 as a TV broadcast transmission tower and opened to the public in the 1980s. Standing 236.7m tall at the 243m summit of Namsan, its actual elevation is 479.7m. Rebranded as N Seoul Tower in 2005, it features an observatory, a rotating observation deck, and restaurants. Its padlock fence is a famous spot for couples.
seoul-013.emotionalDescription: The panoramic view of Seoul from N Seoul Tower is captivating both day and night. By day you appreciate the city's massive scale and urban planning; at night you enjoy a brilliant cityscape lit up with lights. The cable car ride up Namsan is itself a special experience, and the breeze at the top becomes an unforgettable memory.

seoul-014.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
seoul-014.summary: A restored stream running through central Seoul, a successful example of urban regeneration
seoul-014.historicalDescription: Cheonggyecheon Stream was a waterway flowing through the heart of Hanyang in the Joseon era. Covered over in the 1950s–60s to make way for an elevated highway during rapid economic growth, it was restored in 2003 under Seoul Mayor Lee Myung-bak's urban regeneration project and opened in 2005 as one of Seoul's premier recreational spaces.
seoul-014.emotionalDescription: Cheonggyecheon is a special space where Seoul's past and present, nature and city, intersect. Walking along the clear water flowing through the heart of the concrete city, you can feel nature even within the urban environment. The contrasting scenery of nighttime illumination, the sound of water, and surrounding skyscrapers showcases a uniquely Seoul charm.

seoul-015.name: Han River Citizen's Park
seoul-015.summary: A large public park along the Han River, with bike paths and water sports
seoul-015.historicalDescription: Han River Citizen's Park was established as part of the Han River Comprehensive Development Project in the 1980s. Comprising 12 parks from Gangseo to Gwangnaru, the total area exceeds 2.1 million m². During the Joseon era, important ferry crossings were located here. Today it offers bike paths, swimming pools, camping grounds, baseball fields, and many other facilities.
seoul-015.emotionalDescription: Han River Park is the playground and retreat of Seoul's citizens. Cycling or walking along the Han River feeling the river breeze, and enjoying fried chicken and beer at the riverside as the sun sets, is an essential part of Seoul life. At night, the moonlit riverscape and the illumination of bridges create a beautiful scene.

seoul-016.name: Gwanghwamun
seoul-016.summary: The main gate of Gyeongbokgung and a symbol of Seoul, home to the plaza with statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi
seoul-016.historicalDescription: Gwanghwamun is the southern main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace, serving as the main gate since its founding in 1395. During the colonial period it was moved, then relocated again in 1968, and finally restored to its original location in 2010. Gwanghwamun Plaza features statues of King Sejong the Great and Admiral Yi Sun-sin, representing Seoul's central square.
seoul-016.emotionalDescription: Gwanghwamun Plaza is a space where Korea's history and pride coexist. Gazing at the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin, you feel the greatness of Joseon history, and passing through Gwanghwamun to enter Gyeongbokgung is an experience that transcends time and space. The Royal Guard Changing Ceremony showcases traditional culture in living form.
seoul-016.bestTime: All seasons, Royal Guard Changing Ceremony

seoul-017.name: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park
seoul-017.summary: The former Dongdaemun Stadium transformed into a cultural park, where DDP and historic ruins coexist
seoul-017.historicalDescription: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park was established in 2010 after the Dongdaemun Stadium was demolished. Excavations revealed Baekje-era ruins and Joseon-era relics, leading to the creation of a historical park. Operated by the Seoul Design Foundation alongside the DDP (Dongdaemun Design Plaza), it is a space where past and future, history and design, coexist.
seoul-017.emotionalDescription: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park is a unique space where Seoul's past, present, and future converge. Gazing at Baekje-era ruins, you feel Seoul's long history, and viewing the DDP's future-oriented architecture, you can imagine Seoul's leap forward. The nighttime DDP LED roses alongside nearby shopping malls' neon signs showcase the energy of contemporary Seoul.

seoul-018.name: Myeongdong Cathedral
seoul-018.summary: Korea's first Catholic parish church, a beautiful Gothic-style cathedral
seoul-018.historicalDescription: Myeongdong Cathedral was completed in 1898 as Korea's first Catholic parish church. It also carries the weight of history as a site where believers were martyred during Joseon-era Catholic persecutions. A pure Gothic structure built with 450,000 bricks, it features a 23m bell tower. Designated as a National Folk Cultural Heritage in 1977, it currently serves as the seat of the Archdiocese of Seoul.
seoul-018.emotionalDescription: Myeongdong Cathedral is a quiet sanctuary standing in the heart of busy Myeongdong. Within the majestic Gothic architecture and the mystical atmosphere created by stained glass, you can find inner peace. The illuminated exterior at night creates an otherworldly scene within the city, and the weight of being a historic martyrdom site is palpably felt.

seoul-019.name: Seodaemun Prison History Hall
seoul-019.summary: A site of the independence movement during the Japanese colonial period, a place to remember painful history
seoul-019.historicalDescription: Seodaemun Prison was established by the Japanese in 1908 and served as a place to imprison and torture independence fighters until 1945. Countless activists including Kim Gu, Ahn Jung-geun, and Yu Gwan-sun were held here. After liberation it was used as a prison, and in 1992 it opened as a history hall. The preserved prison blocks, cells, and torture chambers bear witness to Japanese oppression.
seoul-019.emotionalDescription: Visiting Seodaemun Prison History Hall is a time to confront painful history and reflect on the sacrifices of independence fighters. Viewing the narrow cells and torture instruments, you can imagine the suffering of the time, and the courage and sacrifice of independence activists evoke deep emotion and reverence. It is a place that makes you realize the preciousness of freedom and independence.

seoul-020.name: Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House)
seoul-020.summary: The former presidential residence, now a historic space open to the public
seoul-020.historicalDescription: Cheong Wa Dae was a royal garden behind Changdeokgung Palace in the Joseon era, used as the governor-general's residence during the colonial period. After liberation it became the presidential residence for 74 years, until the Yoon administration relocated to Yongsan in 2022 and opened it to the public. It features the main building, Yeongbingwan, and Chunchugwan, with beautiful Joseon gardens against a Bugaksan backdrop.
seoul-020.emotionalDescription: Cheong Wa Dae is both a site of modern Korean history and a former symbol of power. Freely exploring a space that was off-limits to the public for decades, you can feel the history of Korean democracy. The beautiful natural scenery of Bugaksan combined with traditional architecture demonstrates its value as a cultural heritage beyond its political significance.

seoul-021.name: Bugaksan Mountain
seoul-021.summary: The mountain guarding northern Seoul, a historic hiking trail along the Seoul City Wall
seoul-021.historicalDescription: Bugaksan is located to the north of Seoul at 342m elevation. During the Joseon Dynasty, the northern section of the Seoul City Wall was built here; it is also known as Baegak. The Bugaksan trail is part of the Hanyangdoseong City Wall Trail, running from Changuimun to Namgajwa-dong. The panoramic view of downtown Seoul from the summit is outstanding.
seoul-021.emotionalDescription: Walking the Bugaksan trail is the quintessential experience of a historical walk within the city. Following the Joseon-era fortress wall, you feel centuries of history, and reaching the summit to overlook Seoul, you marvel at the coexistence of city and nature. The nighttime views of Seoul at sunset are particularly unforgettable.

seoul-022.name: Bukhansan National Park
seoul-022.summary: A renowned mountain in northwestern Seoul, a pilgrimage for hikers and home to numerous Buddhist temples
seoul-022.historicalDescription: Bukhansan, Seoul's guardian mountain, stands at 836.5m and is one of Korea's foremost mountains. Fortifications were built here from the Joseon era, and Bukhansan Fortress (Historic Site No. 162) remains today. Numerous temples including Wonhyosa, Jingwansa, and Doseonsa make it a place of religious significance as well. It was designated a National Park in 1983.
seoul-022.emotionalDescription: Climbing Bukhansan is a time to leave the city behind and commune with nature. The exhilaration of reaching the summit along rocky ridges, and the peace found in the tranquility of temples, helps you forget the stress of everyday life. The view of Seoul from the summit rewards the effort of the climb.

seoul-023.name: Dobongsan Mountain
seoul-023.summary: A famous rocky ridge hiking destination, the iconic peak of northern Seoul
seoul-023.historicalDescription: Dobongsan, at 740m, is located in northeastern Seoul. It holds historical significance as the site of King Jinheung of Silla's inspection stele. Part of Bukhansan National Park, its rocky ridges are especially popular with hiking enthusiasts. Temples such as Mangwolsa and Wondobongsa are also found here.
seoul-023.emotionalDescription: Climbing Dobongsan's rocky ridges provides a thrilling adventure and a sense of achievement. The exhilaration of clearing boulders and ridges to reach a summit with the city spread out below is unforgettable. It is a great course to combine with nearby Bukhansan for extended trekking.

seoul-024.name: Gwanaksan Mountain
seoul-024.summary: A mountain near Seoul National University, an urban mountain with temples and historic sites
seoul-024.historicalDescription: Gwanaksan, at 632m, is located in southern Seoul. It is home to temples including Hoamsa, Yeonjuam, and Yeongoksa, and served as a guardian mountain for the surrounding region in the Joseon era. Adjacent to Seoul National University, it serves as a retreat for students and residents. The summit offers a panoramic view of southern Seoul.
seoul-024.emotionalDescription: Gwanaksan is a familiar mountain steeped in the memories of SNU students. Visiting temples for meditation, or walking along ridges to view the cityscape, you can find peace of mind. Spring azaleas and autumn foliage provide beautiful scenic trails.

seoul-025.name: Seoul Grand Park
seoul-025.summary: A large theme park combining a zoo, botanical garden, and theme gardens — a popular family outing destination
seoul-025.historicalDescription: Seoul Grand Park opened in 1984 as a large comprehensive park. Covering approximately 2.64 million m², it includes a zoo, botanical garden, theme gardens, forest bath, and a lake. It was the site of Joseon-era royal tombs, and though located in Gwacheon, it is managed by the Seoul Metropolitan Government.
seoul-025.emotionalDescription: Seoul Grand Park is perfect for families to enjoy nature together. You can see diverse animals at the zoo, admire seasonal flowers at the botanical garden, and enjoy a picnic on the spacious lawn. It is a place to escape the city and spend healing time in nature.

seoul-026.name: Gwacheon Grand Park
seoul-026.summary: A large natural park adjacent to Seoul Grand Park, ideal for walks and relaxation
seoul-026.historicalDescription: Gwacheon Grand Park is a large urban park established alongside Seoul Grand Park. Developed in the mid-1980s, it features vast lawns, a lake, and walking paths. On weekends it is a popular destination for citizens enjoying picnics and leisure activities.
seoul-026.emotionalDescription: Gwacheon Grand Park's wide lawns are a green oasis within the city. You can picnic with family, stroll by the lakeside to listen to nature's sounds, and enjoy spring cherry blossoms and autumn ginkgo leaves that are especially beautiful.

seoul-027.name: Children's Grand Park
seoul-027.summary: A comprehensive theme park for children, packed with a zoo and amusement facilities
seoul-027.historicalDescription: Children's Grand Park, opened in 1973, is Korea's first comprehensive children's theme park. It was the site of the rear garden of Changgyeonggung Palace and the tomb of Empress Myeongseong in the Joseon era. With a zoo, botanical garden, amusement park, and performance hall, it is beloved as an educational and recreational space for children.
seoul-027.emotionalDescription: Children's Grand Park is a happy space filled with the laughter of children. Learning about the importance of life by seeing various animals, running around in the amusement facilities, and creating precious family memories — the park is endlessly joyful. Leisurely time on the wide lawn is also memorable.

seoul-028.name: Olympic Park
seoul-028.summary: Legacy of the 1988 Seoul Olympics, a park where sports and cultural arts coexist
seoul-028.historicalDescription: Olympic Park was established for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Seoul Olympics. It is also historically significant as the excavation site of Mongchontoseong and Hanseong Baekje ruins. The Olympic Sculpture Park, SOMA Museum of Art, and Olympic Hall make it a space where sports and culture blend.
seoul-028.emotionalDescription: Olympic Park is a space honoring the glory of the '88 Olympics. Strolling among sculptures in the sculpture park to enjoy culture and nature, and walking along Mongchon Lake for a peaceful time — the nighttime illumination and sculptures create a fantastical atmosphere.

seoul-029.name: World Cup Park
seoul-029.summary: Legacy of the 2002 World Cup, an eco-park transformed from the Sangam-dong landfill
seoul-029.historicalDescription: World Cup Park was established to commemorate the 2002 FIFA World Cup. After the Sangam-dong landfill, in use from 1978 to 1993, was closed, it was transformed into an eco-park. Comprising five themed parks — Sky Park, Sunset Park, Peace Park, and others — it is cited as a successful example of ecological restoration.
seoul-029.emotionalDescription: Sky Park's silver grass fields are Seoul's representative autumn highlight. Witnessing beautiful nature reborn from what was once a landfill, you feel the importance of the environment, and the sunset view of the Han River from Sunset Park is an unforgettable scene. It is a place that shows the hope of ecological restoration.

seoul-030.name: Seokchon Lake
seoul-030.summary: Jamsil's signature lake park, an urban lake harmonizing with Lotte World Tower
seoul-030.historicalDescription: Seokchon Lake, called Punggukji in the Joseon era, was connected to Songpanaruteo ferry crossing, serving as a transportation and agricultural water source. Developed alongside the Jamsil area in the 1980s, it is now a beloved recreational space for citizens. Together with Lotte World Tower, it has become a landmark of Songpa.
seoul-030.emotionalDescription: Seokchon Lake represents the modern urban landscape with Lotte World Tower. Walking along the lakeside and gazing at the city skyline, and in the evening enjoying the fantastic night views created by the tower and its lake reflection — spring cherry blossoms provide a beautiful promenade.

gyeonggi-001.name: Hwaseong Fortress
gyeonggi-001.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the crowning achievement of King Jeongjo's ambitious urban planning
gyeonggi-001.historicalDescription: Hwaseong Fortress was built in 1794 when King Jeongjo moved the tomb of his father, Prince Sado, and planned Suwon as a new city. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997, it was designed by Jeong Yak-yong with both scientific structure and beautiful architecture. Features include Janganmun Gate, Seobuk Gongsindeon, and Hwaseomun Gate.
gyeonggi-001.emotionalDescription: Walking Hwaseong Fortress is a journey experiencing the finest urban planning of the Joseon era. Strolling along the fortress walls, you feel King Jeongjo's ambition and the touching bond between father and son, and the grandeur of Hwaseong Haenggung and the lively atmosphere of the plaza in front provide a special experience where history and the present coexist.

gyeonggi-002.name: Hwaseong Haenggung
gyeonggi-002.summary: King Jeongjo's temporary royal residence, a grand palace within Hwaseong Fortress
gyeonggi-002.historicalDescription: Hwaseong Haenggung was built in 1789 as a temporary palace for King Jeongjo to stay in when visiting Hwaseong. It served as the administrative center of the new city Suwon, and features Bongsudang Hall where King Jeongjo enshrined the portrait of his father Prince Sado. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site together with Hwaseong Fortress, traditional performances are regularly held here.
gyeonggi-002.emotionalDescription: Hwaseong Haenggung is a space where you can feel King Jeongjo's virtue. Walking through the grand pavilions and gardens, you sense the dignity of the Joseon royal family, and at Bongsudang you can be immersed in the historical weight of the bond between King Jeongjo and Prince Sado. Regular performances showcase living traditional culture.

gyeonggi-003.name: Imjingak
gyeonggi-003.summary: A DMZ peace landmark, a tourist attraction symbolizing the hope for reunification
gyeonggi-003.historicalDescription: Imjingak was established in 1972 as a peace tourism area near the northern limit line. A space to commemorate the devastation of the Korean War and hope for reunification, it includes the Freedom Bridge, Unification Park, and the Mangbaedan Altar. Redeveloped as a modern tourist site in the 2000s, it is also the starting point for DMZ tours.
gyeonggi-003.emotionalDescription: Imjingak is where the pain of division and the hope for reunification intersect. Gazing at the Freedom Bridge, you feel the sorrow of separated families, and at the Mangbaedan Altar, praying for reunification, you can empathize with the national sentiment. The symbolic sculptures in the nearby Pyeonghwanuri Park convey a message of hope.

gyeonggi-004.name: Paju Book City
gyeonggi-004.summary: Asia's largest publishing culture complex, the Street of Wisdom
gyeonggi-004.historicalDescription: Paju Book City began in 1989 and was developed in earnest from the 1990s as a publishing culture specialized city. World-renowned architects participated in creating distinctive buildings, and it is densely packed with publishers, bookstores, print shops, and cultural facilities. It continues to develop as a hub of the knowledge industry.
gyeonggi-004.emotionalDescription: Book City is a space filled with the fragrance of books and wisdom. Walking between beautiful buildings, visiting bookstores and galleries, and reading a book in a quiet café — you can enjoy intellectual leisure. Various cultural events and exhibitions make it a vibrant center of arts and culture.

gyeonggi-005.name: Heyri Art Village
gyeonggi-005.summary: An artists' village where galleries and cafes coexist, a vibrant cultural arts space
gyeonggi-005.historicalDescription: Heyri was founded in 1997 by cultural artists who gathered to create an arts village. Modeled on Germany's Bauhaus, architects, sculptors, painters, and writers created unique spaces. Distinctive buildings, galleries, cafes, and performance venues blend together in a space where art and nature coexist.
gyeonggi-005.emotionalDescription: Heyri is a special space created by the passion of artists. Walking among distinctive buildings, visiting galleries, and leisurely sipping tea in a garden, you can feel the energy of creativity. Various cultural events and exhibitions make it a vibrant artistic community.

gyeonggi-006.name: Dumulmeori (Confluence of Two Rivers)
gyeonggi-006.summary: Where the South Han River meets the North Han River, a beautiful natural scenic spot
gyeonggi-006.historicalDescription: Dumulmeori is where the South Han River and North Han River converge — the name itself means 'two waters meeting.' It has been a transportation hub since the Goryeo Dynasty, and in modern times was partially submerged with the construction of Paldang Dam. Today it is Yangpyeong's premier tourist destination alongside Paldang Bridge.
gyeonggi-006.emotionalDescription: The view of the rivers converging at Dumulmeori is spectacular. Feeling the greatness of nature in the scene of clear waters meeting, you can spend leisurely time by the riverside. The scenery at sunrise and sunset is particularly a favorite spot for photographers.

gyeonggi-007.name: Namhansanseong Fortress
gyeonggi-007.summary: The representative Joseon mountain fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage historic site
gyeonggi-007.historicalDescription: Namhansanseong Fortress was built during King Injo's reign in 1624 and is famous as the refuge of King Injo during the Manchu invasion of 1636. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014, 12km of fortress walls, four main gates, and various military facilities are preserved. Major structures include the Sueo Jangdae Command Post and Janggyeongsa Temple.
gyeonggi-007.emotionalDescription: Walking Namhansanseong is experiencing the history of the last resistance and national calamity of the Joseon era. Walking the fortress walls, you recall the stories of King Injo and the Cheokwabi Stele, and the view from the summit makes you viscerally appreciate the fortress's strategic value. A place to heal in nature while feeling the weight of history.

gyeonggi-008.name: Korean Folk Village
gyeonggi-008.summary: A theme park where you can experience Korean traditional culture, a vivid recreation of a folk village
gyeonggi-008.historicalDescription: Korean Folk Village opened in 1974 as a traditional culture theme park. Displaying over 270 traditional buildings relocated from across the country and folk materials, it provides various experience programs including traditional crafts, folk performances, and traditional wedding ceremonies. It vividly recreates the appearance of a Joseon-era village, serving as a site for education and tourism.
gyeonggi-008.emotionalDescription: Korean Folk Village offers an experience like time-traveling to the Joseon era. Wearing hanbok and walking through the alleyways to experience traditional culture, and watching folk performances, you can deeply empathize with the lives and culture of our ancestors. A great place for families to learn and enjoy tradition together.

gyeonggi-009.name: Everland
gyeonggi-009.summary: Korea's largest theme park, an amusement park with diverse attractions and a zoo
gyeonggi-009.historicalDescription: Everland opened in 1976 as a natural farm and now operates as Samsung's comprehensive theme park. It features five themed zones, a zoo, and a water park (Caribbean Bay), and is Korea's representative amusement park. Four-seasons festivals and parades are its hallmarks.
gyeonggi-009.emotionalDescription: Everland is a space where children's dreams and adults' fantasies coexist. The thrill of various attractions, interaction at the zoo, and beautiful gardens across the seasons bring joy to all ages. The nighttime parade and fireworks offer a truly magical experience.

gyeonggi-010.name: Caribbean Bay
gyeonggi-010.summary: A large water park adjacent to Everland, with indoor and outdoor water facilities available year-round
gyeonggi-010.historicalDescription: Caribbean Bay is a large water park that opened in 1996, adjacent to Everland. It features indoor and outdoor pools, various water slides, wave pools, and spa facilities, and operates year-round with heated indoor pools in winter. Its surfing zone and wave pool are highlights.
gyeonggi-010.emotionalDescription: Caribbean Bay offers fun and coolness on hot summer days. Riding the waves in the wave pool blows off stress, and the thrill of various slides is exhilarating. In winter, you can relax soaking in warm water at the indoor spa.

gyeonggi-011.name: Sanjeonghose (Mountain Lake)
gyeonggi-011.summary: A beautiful lake surrounded by mountains, popular for its observatory and walking trails
gyeonggi-011.historicalDescription: Sanjeonghose is an artificial lake in Pocheon, renowned for its exceptional scenery blending with the surrounding mountains. Originally created as an agricultural reservoir, it developed into a tourist destination. The lake observatory, walking trails, and monorail make it popular with family visitors.
gyeonggi-011.emotionalDescription: Sanjeonghose offers beautiful scenery where mountains and lake meet. Walking along the trails breathing fresh air, the view of the lake from the observatory puts the mind at ease. The autumn foliage scenery is particularly spectacular.

gyeonggi-012.name: Jarasum Island
gyeonggi-012.summary: An island on the Bukhan River, a cultural tourist spot famous for its jazz festival
gyeonggi-012.historicalDescription: Jarasum is an inland island formed during North Han River construction works. Originally a barren strip of land, it was developed by Gapyeong County into a park. The Jarasum International Jazz Festival has been held annually since 2004, earning it fame as an island of music.
gyeonggi-012.emotionalDescription: Jarasum is a romantic space where music and nature meet. Surrounded by the river and trees of the island, you can listen to jazz music and spend leisurely time. During the jazz festival, you can enjoy performances by world-class musicians.

gyeonggi-013.name: Nami Island
gyeonggi-013.summary: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, a tourist island famous as a drama filming location
gyeonggi-013.historicalDescription: Nami Island is a crescent-shaped island on the North Han River. Designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2006, it rose to fame as the filming location for the drama 'Winter Sonata.' Its metasequoia tree-lined road is particularly famous.
gyeonggi-013.emotionalDescription: Nami Island offers the romance of feeling like the protagonist of a drama. Walking through the metasequoia tree tunnel, admiring the changing scenery across seasons, and experiencing childlike wonder at the UNICEF Children's Park — it is a place that creates memories for families and couples alike.

gyeonggi-014.name: Cheongpyeong Lake
gyeonggi-014.summary: An upper Han River lake, a destination for water leisure and healing
gyeonggi-014.historicalDescription: Cheongpyeong Lake is a lake formed in the upper Han River by the construction of Cheongpyeong Dam. It developed as a hub for water skiing and boating, and has recently gained popularity as a healing and resort destination. Many pension accommodations and resorts have been built in the surrounding area.
gyeonggi-014.emotionalDescription: Cheongpyeong Lake is a healing space where clear water and mountain scenery blend. Walking along the lakeshore or enjoying water sports, you can relieve stress in nature. The harmony of the lake's tranquility and the mountain's grandeur creates a therapeutic view.

gyeonggi-015.name: Hwadamsup Arboretum
gyeonggi-015.summary: A large arboretum to enjoy with a monorail through beautiful forest
gyeonggi-015.historicalDescription: Hwadamsup Arboretum opened in 2013 and is located in Gwangju, Gyeonggi. It displays over 4,800 plant species and features a monorail for viewing the forest, making it especially popular with families. It offers different landscapes across the four seasons.
gyeonggi-015.emotionalDescription: Hwadamsup is a space to escape the city and commune with nature. Riding the monorail to soar above the forest admiring the seasonal scenery, and walking the trails to encounter diverse plants — the autumn foliage waves are particularly spectacular.

gyeonggi-016.name: Garden of Morning Calm
gyeonggi-016.summary: Korea's representative arboretum, popular for its beautiful themed gardens and walking trails
gyeonggi-016.historicalDescription: The Garden of Morning Calm was established in 1996 by Professor Han Sang-kyung. Over 5,000 plant species are displayed across 20 themed gardens, with walking trails, ponds, and observation decks. Various flower festivals are held each season, and spring cherry blossoms, azaleas, and autumn foliage are particularly famous.
gyeonggi-016.emotionalDescription: The Garden of Morning Calm is a place to experience the art of gardening. Strolling through themed gardens to admire seasonal flowers and trees, and meditating by a quiet pond, soothes the soul. It is a perfect space for a walk with someone special.

gyeonggi-017.name: Byeokchoji Garden
gyeonggi-017.summary: An arboretum where European-style and Korean traditional gardens coexist
gyeonggi-017.historicalDescription: Byeokchoji Garden is a large arboretum in Paju featuring both European-style and Korean traditional gardens. With over 1,300 plant species, it includes themed gardens such as a rose garden, hydrangea garden, and herb garden. It is also known as a drama filming location.
gyeonggi-017.emotionalDescription: Byeokchoji Garden is a space where the beauty of Eastern and Western gardens coexist. Walking through a rose garden in full bloom feeling European romance, and finding quiet in the Korean traditional garden — flowers blooming at different times throughout the seasons bring fresh emotion with each visit.

gyeonggi-018.name: Daejanggeum Park
gyeonggi-018.summary: Film set of the drama 'Jewel in the Palace,' an experiential space for Korean traditional culture
gyeonggi-018.historicalDescription: Daejanggeum Park is the filming location for MBC dramas including 'Jewel in the Palace,' 'Dong Yi,' and 'Yi San,' converted into a tourist attraction. Joseon-era palaces, commoner houses, and markets have been recreated, allowing visitors to experience the drama's settings. Hanbok experience and traditional craft experiences are available.
gyeonggi-018.emotionalDescription: Daejanggeum Park is a place to directly experience drama scenes. Viewing the Joseon-era palace and recalling iconic drama scenes, wearing hanbok to take photos and create memories — it is a great place for a light experience of Korean traditional culture.

gyeonggi-019.name: Icheon Rice Museum
gyeonggi-019.summary: A specialized museum showcasing everything about rice culture
gyeonggi-019.historicalDescription: Icheon Rice Museum is a specialized museum located in Icheon, a major rice-producing area of Korea. It displays the history of rice, cultivation processes, farming tools, and foods made from rice. Icheon has been famous as a rice-producing area since the Joseon era and remains synonymous with high-quality rice today.
gyeonggi-019.emotionalDescription: The Rice Museum is a place to deepen understanding of rice, the staple food of Koreans. You can feel the wisdom and effort of our farmers, taste various rice-based dishes, and reflect on the importance of agricultural culture. An educational space for contemplating the value of farming culture.

gyeonggi-020.name: King Sejong's Royal Tomb (Yeongneung)
gyeonggi-020.summary: The royal tomb of King Sejong, creator of Hangul, the pinnacle of Joseon royal tombs
gyeonggi-020.historicalDescription: Yeongneung is the royal tomb of King Sejong the Great, who created Hangul and ushered in the golden age of Joseon culture, and of Queen Soheon. Relocated from Seoul to its current site in 1970, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Joseon Royal Tombs in 2009. The Joseon garden within the tomb complex is beautiful.
gyeonggi-020.emotionalDescription: Yeongneung is a sacred space honoring a great king. Walking through the beautiful forested path along the trails and reflecting on King Sejong's achievements, you can appreciate the preciousness of Hangul. Within the beauty of the Joseon garden, you feel a sense of awe.

gyeonggi-021.name: Namhansanseong Fortress, Gwangju Section
gyeonggi-021.summary: A section of the historic Namhansanseong Fortress accessible from Gwangju, combining history and scenic trekking
gyeonggi-021.historicalDescription: The Gwangju section of Namhansanseong is the southern portion of the fortress accessible from Gwangju City. It includes Sueo Jangdae (a military command post) and several fortress gates, connected to well-maintained trekking routes popular with hikers. The fortress walls were the site of Joseon's last stand against the Qing invasion of 1636.
gyeonggi-021.emotionalDescription: The hiking trail through Namhansanseong starting from Gwangju is a course where history and nature intertwine. Walking along the fortress walls and reflecting on their historical significance, the panoramic views from the ramparts reward every step of the climb.

gyeonggi-022.name: Hoeamsa Temple Site, Yangju
gyeonggi-022.summary: An ancient temple founded in the Silla era, renowned for its historic grounds and stone artifacts
gyeonggi-022.historicalDescription: Hoeamsa Temple was founded during the Silla period and received royal patronage during the Joseon era. Only the temple grounds remain today, but the preserved Goryeo and Joseon-era stone artifacts hold great academic value. The Yangju Hoeamsa Temple Site is designated Historic Site No. 128.
gyeonggi-022.emotionalDescription: The Hoeamsa temple site is a quiet space where a thousand years of history can be felt. Looking at the remaining stone artifacts and imagining the scale of the former temple, you can sense the weight of history in this peaceful setting.

gyeonggi-023.name: Jeongok-ri Paleolithic Site, Yeoncheon
gyeonggi-023.summary: East Asia's oldest known paleolithic site — a window into the very dawn of human prehistory
gyeonggi-023.historicalDescription: The Jeongok-ri Paleolithic Site, excavated in 1978, is known as the oldest paleolithic site in East Asia. Traces of human life dating back hundreds of thousands of years are preserved here, making it of worldwide academic significance. It was designated National Treasure No. 443 in 2011.
gyeonggi-023.emotionalDescription: The Jeongok-ri site is where you encounter the beginning of human history. Walking the ground where ancestors lived hundreds of thousands of years ago, you feel the mystery of human evolution, and through the excavated artifacts you can imagine the lives of ancient people.

gangwon-001.name: Woljeongsa Temple, Odaesan
gangwon-001.summary: A thousand-year-old temple nestled in Odaesan, guardian of the Tripitaka Koreana
gangwon-001.historicalDescription: Woljeongsa Temple was founded in 643 CE by Monk Jajang and holds a millennium of history stretching back to the Silla Dynasty. It houses the Gyeongpanjeon, which stored the Tripitaka Koreana, registered as a UNESCO Memory of the World in 2000. The fir tree forest path is famous, and the temple is located within Odaesan National Park.
gangwon-001.emotionalDescription: Walking the fir tree forest path at Woljeongsa is a soul-purifying experience. Moving beneath towering trees you feel profound stillness, and within the atmosphere of this thousand-year-old temple you find peace of mind. Winter snow scenes create a truly mystical ambiance.

gangwon-002.name: Sinheungsa Temple, Seoraksan
gangwon-002.summary: Seoraksan's foremost temple, blending millennium-old history with spectacular mountain scenery
gangwon-002.historicalDescription: Sinheungsa Temple was founded in 637 CE by Monk Jajang and is the principal temple of Seoraksan. It received royal patronage during the Joseon Dynasty and was destroyed during the Korean War before being restored. Located within Seoraksan National Park, it is popular with hikers.
gangwon-002.emotionalDescription: Sinheungsa is a serene temple harmonized with the grand nature of Seoraksan. The majestic mountain scenery viewed from the temple overwhelms the senses, and the sound of the crystal-clear valley stream invites meditation. It is a sacred space where nature and religion meet.

gangwon-003.name: Gyeongpodae Pavilion, Gangneung
gangwon-003.summary: A centuries-old pavilion overlooking Gyeongpo Lake and the East Sea — Gangneung's beloved landmark
gangwon-003.historicalDescription: Gyeongpodae Pavilion was built in 1322 during the late Goryeo period. Situated to overlook both Gyeongpo Lake and the East Sea simultaneously, it is known as the childhood home of Sin Saimdang. It was a famous spot where many Joseon-era literati wrote poetry. The current structure was restored in 1984.
gangwon-003.emotionalDescription: Climbing Gyeongpodae and gazing out over Gyeongpo Lake and the East Sea is the highlight of any Gangneung trip. The panorama where the broad ripples of Gyeongpo Lake meet the sea is spectacular, and the sunrise in particular creates unforgettable memories. It is a place where you can feel the artistic spirit of Sin Saimdang.

gangwon-004.name: Ojukheon House, Gangneung
gangwon-004.summary: Birthplace of Sin Saimdang and Yulgok Yi I — a quintessential Joseon hanok cultural heritage
gangwon-004.historicalDescription: Ojukheon is the birthplace of both the Joseon Confucian scholar Yulgok Yi I and his mother Sin Saimdang. Named for the black bamboo (ojuk) growing on its grounds, the main hall and surrounding structures were restored in 1963. Munseongsa shrine on the property exhibits artifacts of both Yulgok and Sin Saimdang.
gangwon-004.emotionalDescription: Ojukheon is a place where the story of Korea's greatest mother and son still lives. Strolling through the garden dense with black bamboo, you can sense Sin Saimdang's artistic talent and passion for education alongside Yulgok's scholarly achievements. It is a beautiful space where traditional Korean architecture and garden aesthetics unite.

gangwon-005.name: Seongyojang Estate, Gangneung
gangwon-005.summary: A representative Joseon-era private garden villa — the best-preserved aristocratic garden in Korea
gangwon-005.historicalDescription: Seongyojang was built as a villa in 1828 by Han Se-gyeom, a provincial governor of the Joseon era. Covering approximately 16,000㎡, the grounds harmoniously combine a pond, pavilions, and towers, showcasing the beauty of Joseon garden design. It is regarded as the best-preserved example of a Joseon-era private garden still in existence.
gangwon-005.emotionalDescription: Seongyojang is a place where the pinnacle of Joseon garden aesthetics is on display. Among the harmony of pavilions and trees surrounding the pond, you can imagine the leisure that Joseon scholars felt. The natural arrangement of the garden conveys the philosophy of Eastern garden design.

gangwon-006.name: Gangneung Coffee Street
gangwon-006.summary: Gangneung's iconic café district by the sea at Anmok — Korea's coffee culture capital
gangwon-006.historicalDescription: Gangneung Coffee Street developed from the 2000s as cafés gathered along Gangneung's beautiful coastline. Anmok in particular, originally the site of a coffee factory, now blends a coffee museum with cafés. Gangneung has established itself as the most famous coffee culture city in Korea.
gangwon-006.emotionalDescription: Gangneung Coffee Street is where the romance of the sea and coffee converge. A cup of coffee enjoyed while watching East Sea waves from a café washes away the fatigue of daily life. The sunrise viewed from Anmok is especially a must-do stop on any Gangneung trip.

gangwon-007.name: Seoraksan Mountain, Sokcho
gangwon-007.summary: Korea's most iconic mountain — the Sokcho gateway into Seoraksan National Park
gangwon-007.historicalDescription: Seoraksan was designated a national park in 1970 and is the most representative mountain in Korea. The approach from Sokcho, called Outer Seorak, links with hiking trails around Sinheungsa Temple. It features diverse peaks including Ulsanbawi Rock and Dinosaur Ridge, and was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1982.
gangwon-007.emotionalDescription: Seoraksan is a mysterious mountain where majestic rocky ridges and deep valleys intertwine. Walking the hiking trails, you are overwhelmed by the grandeur of nature, and the view of Ulsanbawi Rock and the East Sea from the summit makes every effort worthwhile. It shows a different beauty in every season.

gangwon-008.name: Yeongeumjeong Pavilion, Sokcho
gangwon-008.summary: A pavilion built over the sea in Sokcho, one of the East Coast's finest sunrise viewing spots
gangwon-008.historicalDescription: Yeongeumjeong Pavilion was built at Sokcho Beach in 1988. Set directly over the water, it allows close-up views of waves crashing against the shore and is renowned as a sunrise spot. Its beautiful silhouette merged with the sea attracts many visitors.
gangwon-008.emotionalDescription: Yeongeumjeong is the pavilion closest to the sea. Listening to the sound of the waves and gazing at the ocean, watching the sun rise over the golden sea at dawn is an unforgettable experience. It is a place where you can fully feel the romance of Sokcho's coast.

gangwon-009.name: Sokcho Jungang Market
gangwon-009.summary: Sokcho's signature traditional market, famous for seasoned fried chicken and fresh seafood
gangwon-009.historicalDescription: Sokcho Jungang Market has been the city's representative market since the 1960s. Originally centered on seafood, it has evolved into a comprehensive market combining Sokcho's signature seasoned fried chicken alley, a raw fish center, and traditional street food. It is a popular destination for both tourists and locals alike.
gangwon-009.emotionalDescription: Sokcho Jungang Market is where you feel the liveliness of the East Coast. Comparing different seasoned fried chicken stalls, enjoying fresh seafood at the raw fish center, and experiencing Sokcho's food culture is a delight. The warmth of people and the vibrant market atmosphere give it a special charm.

gangwon-010.name: Sunrise Park, Donghae
gangwon-010.summary: The East Coast's finest sunrise spot, beloved for its Wish Stairs and sweeping ocean views
gangwon-010.historicalDescription: Sunrise Park is a major tourist attraction in Donghae City and one of the most beautiful spots on the East Coast to watch the sunrise. Established in 1998, it features the Wish Stairs, an outdoor amphitheater, and an observation deck. A New Year sunrise event is held every January 1st.
gangwon-010.emotionalDescription: Sunrise Park is a place where many people come on New Year's Day to make their wishes. Climbing the Wish Stairs while thinking of new hopes, and watching the sun rise over the East Coast from the summit warms the heart. It is a special experience to be among the first in Korea to see the sunrise.

gangwon-011.name: Samcheok Maritime Cable Car
gangwon-011.summary: Korea's longest sea cable car, delivering sweeping views of the East Coast's dramatic scenery
gangwon-011.historicalDescription: The Samcheok Maritime Cable Car, opened in 2008, is Korea's longest sea cable car at 3.74km. It links Jangho Port with the mainland, offering panoramic views of the East Coast's spectacular scenery. A crystal-floor cruise gondola is also operated and is very popular.
gangwon-011.emotionalDescription: The Samcheok Maritime Cable Car offers the special experience of admiring the grand East Coast scenery from the sky. Soaring over the sea and marveling at the pristine blue waters and coastal cliffs, looking down through the transparent floor gives a breathtaking thrill.

gangwon-012.name: Jangho Port, Samcheok
gangwon-012.summary: A beautiful fishing harbor on the East Coast, famed for its emerald-green waters
gangwon-012.historicalDescription: Jangho Port is a beautiful fishing village harbor in Samcheok. The emerald-green waters of the pristine sea combined with the charm of the fishing village make it popular with visitors. It is connected to the cable car line and has a coastal walking path along the shoreline.
gangwon-012.emotionalDescription: Jangho Port is charming for its emerald sea and the quaint scenery of the fishing village. Walking around the harbor while admiring the crystal-clear waters, and soaring above the sea on the cable car, you can have a truly special experience. It is a hidden gem of the East Coast.

gangwon-013.name: Arirang Market, Jeongseon
gangwon-013.summary: The signature market of Arirang's hometown, Jeongseon, bursting with local food and folk culture
gangwon-013.historicalDescription: Jeongseon Arirang Market is the representative traditional market of Jeongseon, reflecting the character of Arirang's hometown. Modernized in the 2000s, it sells Jeongseon's specialties including gondeure rice, ddeokme (pounded rice cake), and hwanggi root. Arirang performances and experience programs are also offered.
gangwon-013.emotionalDescription: Arirang Market is a place where you feel the soul of Jeongseon. Listening to Arirang songs while tasting gondeure rice and ddeokme, you can feel the warmth of the Jeongseon people. The nostalgic mountain market atmosphere gives a special feeling that you cannot find in the city.

gangwon-014.name: Hwamdong Cave, Jeongseon
gangwon-014.summary: Korea's most spectacular limestone cave, featuring breathtaking golden stalactites and an underground lake
gangwon-014.historicalDescription: Hwamdong Cave is a large limestone cave opened to the public in 1998. Stretching 1,800m in length, it is characterized by its golden stalactites. The cave was once a gold mine, giving it the name Hwaam. Dramatic lighting inside creates a mystical underground atmosphere.
gangwon-014.emotionalDescription: Hwamdong Cave is a work of art created by nature. Walking among the golden stalactites and marveling at the mystery of the underground world, the reflections in the cave lake present a fantastical landscape. Its constant temperature of 12°C inside also makes it a popular summer retreat.

gangwon-015.name: Daegwallyeong Pass, Pyeongchang
gangwon-015.summary: A scenic highland pass on the Taebaek Range, famous for sheep farms and open meadow vistas
gangwon-015.historicalDescription: Daegwallyeong Pass is a pass through the Taebaek Mountains at 832m elevation. It was an important route connecting the Yeongdong and Yeongseo regions in the Joseon era, and today is famous for its sheep ranch and goat farm. Some events of the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics were held in this area.
gangwon-015.emotionalDescription: Daegwallyeong is a beautiful highland where mountains and pastures come together. Interacting with sheep at the sheep ranch and gazing at the vast meadows gives a feeling of freedom. Both the lush green summer meadows and the snow-covered winter landscape are equally beautiful.

gangwon-016.name: Phoenix Pyeongchang (Phoenix Park)
gangwon-016.summary: A premier four-season resort with ski slopes and golf courses — an Olympic legacy destination
gangwon-016.historicalDescription: Phoenix Pyeongchang opened in 1995 as a four-season resort. It operates a ski slope in winter and a golf course in summer with various amenities. Some events of the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics were held here, and its iPark Ski Slope boasts top-tier facilities in Korea.
gangwon-016.emotionalDescription: Phoenix Pyeongchang is a comprehensive resort offering activities for all four seasons. In winter you can enjoy skiing and snowboarding, in summer golf and relaxation. Surrounded by Pyeongchang's nature and the comfortable atmosphere of the resort, it offers a truly special vacation.

gangwon-017.name: Vivaldi Park, Hongcheon
gangwon-017.summary: Hongcheon's flagship resort, featuring Korea's largest water park and a popular ski slope
gangwon-017.historicalDescription: Vivaldi Park opened in 2006 as a comprehensive resort. It features a ski slope, a water park (Ocean World), and a golf course. Ocean World in particular is famous as the largest water park in Korea. The resort complex is set against the natural backdrop of Hongcheon.
gangwon-017.emotionalDescription: Vivaldi Park is a leisure destination with entertainment for all four seasons. In winter, enjoy skiing and snowboarding; in summer, feel the cool refreshment of Ocean World. The resort's wide range of facilities combined with Hongcheon's natural scenery provides the perfect family vacation.

gangwon-018.name: Soyang River, Chuncheon
gangwon-018.summary: Chuncheon's lifeline — the beautiful river encompassing Lake Uiam and the famous Soyang Dam
gangwon-018.historicalDescription: The Soyang River is a tributary of the Han River that flows through downtown Chuncheon. The construction of the Soyang Dam in 1973 created Lake Uiam. The Lake Uiam Skywalk and Soyang Dam are major tourist attractions, and the Soyang River Girl statue is a symbol of Chuncheon.
gangwon-018.emotionalDescription: The Soyang River is the river that symbolizes the natural beauty of Chuncheon. The view of the lake from the Lake Uiam Skywalk is spectacular, and strolling along the riverside lets you feel the tranquility that Chuncheon is famous for. The sad legend of the Soyang River Girl adds romance to the river.

gangwon-019.name: Nami Island (Chuncheon Section)
gangwon-019.summary: A quiet inland island on the Han River near Chuncheon, ideal for cycling and riverside strolls
gangwon-019.historicalDescription: Chuncheon's Nami Island is a small island in the Chuncheon section of the Han River — a different location from the famous Gapyeong Nami Island. It offers a space to enjoy Chuncheon's natural beauty and is connected to bicycle paths, making it popular as a cycling route.
gangwon-019.emotionalDescription: Chuncheon's Nami Island is a quiet sanctuary on the Han River. Cycling or strolling while enjoying the riverside scenery, the view of Chuncheon's nature from the island puts the mind at ease. It is a hidden gem among Chuncheon's travel destinations.

gangwon-020.name: Kim Yu-jeong Literary Village, Chuncheon
gangwon-020.summary: A cultural space honoring novelist Kim Yu-jeong — Chuncheon's signature literary destination
gangwon-020.historicalDescription: Kim Yu-jeong Literary Village is a cultural space created to honor Chuncheon-born writer Kim Yu-jeong. Opened in 2002, it exhibits his life and works. There are sculptures and exhibits themed around his stories such as 'Camellia' and 'Gold-Digging Bean Field.'
gangwon-020.emotionalDescription: Kim Yu-jeong Literary Village is a place where you can breathe in the scent of Korean modern literature. Walking through scenes from his novels and immersing yourself in Kim Yu-jeong's literary world, you can feel the spirit of Chuncheon that the author loved. It is a special space for those who love literature.

chungcheong-001.name: Gongsanseong Fortress, Gongju
chungcheong-001.summary: A Baekje-era mountain fortress where citadel walls meet the Geumgang River in a historic landscape
chungcheong-001.historicalDescription: Gongsanseong is a mountain fortress built during the Baekje era and was the site of Baekje's last resistance when Goguryeo attacked in 475 CE. The Geumgang River flows below the fortress, creating a beautiful scene alongside the walls. Designated a Historic Site in 1963, the Goransa Temple and pond within the fortress are famous.
chungcheong-001.emotionalDescription: Gongsanseong is the place where Baekje made its final stand in history. Walking along the fortress walls and recalling Baekje's tragedy, the view of the Geumgang River below makes you feel the fortress's strategic importance. Spring cherry blossoms and autumn foliage create a beautiful walking course.

chungcheong-002.name: Naseong Earthen Rampart, Buyeo
chungcheong-002.summary: A Baekje-era earthen defensive wall encircling Buyeo — an important example of ancient earthworks
chungcheong-002.historicalDescription: Naseong is an earthen rampart built during the Baekje era as a defensive structure surrounding Buyeo. Stretching 1.6km, remnants of the earthen walls remain. It was designated a Historic Site in 1975 and is an important relic demonstrating Baekje-era earthworks construction techniques.
chungcheong-002.emotionalDescription: Naseong is a place where you can feel the lives of people in the Baekje era. Walking along the earthen walls and imagining Baekje daily life, you can sense the flow of history in the tranquil atmosphere of Buyeo Town.

chungcheong-003.name: Jeongnimsaji Temple Site, Buyeo
chungcheong-003.summary: A Baekje-era temple ruins with a UNESCO-listed five-story stone pagoda — a jewel of early Korean Buddhism
chungcheong-003.historicalDescription: Jeongnimsaji is the site of a Baekje-era temple, believed to have been founded around the time of the capital's relocation to Sabi in 538 CE. The five-story stone pagoda and stone seated Buddha remain, and the pagoda was designated a National Treasure in 1963. In 2015 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Baekje Historic Districts.
chungcheong-003.emotionalDescription: Jeongnimsaji was once the center of Baekje Buddhism. Looking at the five-story stone pagoda and imagining Baekje Buddhist culture, you can feel the devotion of the Baekje people in the remaining stone structures. In the quiet temple grounds you can be absorbed in the weight of history.

chungcheong-004.name: Yeonmisan Mountain, Nonsan
chungcheong-004.summary: Nonsan's signature mountain featuring a historic fortress, temples, and a national treasure stone pagoda
chungcheong-004.historicalDescription: Yeonmisan is the representative mountain of Nonsan at 222m elevation. A mountain fortress was built on it, and it is home to the Tappeong-ri Seven-Story Stone Pagoda, Gaetaesa Temple, and Ssanggyesa Temple. The Tappeong-ri Seven-Story Pagoda in particular, designated National Treasure No. 143, showcases the architectural beauty of the Silla era.
chungcheong-004.emotionalDescription: Yeonmisan is a place where you can enjoy both the nature and history of Nonsan. Walking the trails to visit the temples and marveling at the beauty of the seven-story pagoda, this quiet mountain offers a perfect healing walking course.

chungcheong-005.name: Cheongnammae (Blue House South), Cheongju
chungcheong-005.summary: The former presidential retreat turned public park, set against the stunning backdrop of Lake Daecheong
chungcheong-005.historicalDescription: Cheongnammae was a presidential retreat built in 1983 during the presidency of Chun Doo-hwan. It was opened to the public in 2003 during the presidency of Roh Moo-hyun, and now operates as a park. The observation deck with Lake Daecheong as its backdrop and the Joseon-style garden are particularly beautiful.
chungcheong-005.emotionalDescription: Cheongnammae is a space that was once a symbol of power but has returned to the people. You can admire the beautiful scenery with Lake Daecheong as a backdrop and take a leisurely stroll through the Joseon-style garden. It is a place that makes you feel the changing tides of history.

chungcheong-006.name: Sapgyoho Lake, Yesan
chungcheong-006.summary: Yesan's signature lake, popular for its dazzling musical fountain — one of the world's largest
chungcheong-006.historicalDescription: Sapgyoho Lake is a reservoir created in 1932 by damming the Sapgyo Stream. In 2012, one of the world's largest musical fountains was installed, attracting visitors from across Korea. There are lakeside walking paths and an observation deck, making it popular with families.
chungcheong-006.emotionalDescription: Sapgyoho Lake is a place to enjoy a symphony of music and water. Experiencing the fantastic atmosphere of the evening musical fountain show and strolling along the lakeshore at a relaxed pace are the highlights of Yesan's representative leisure destination.

chungcheong-007.name: Mallipo Beach, Taean
chungcheong-007.summary: The West Coast's premier beach, famous for spectacular sunsets and calm family-friendly waters
chungcheong-007.historicalDescription: Mallipo Beach opened in 1933 as the West Coast's representative beach. With 2km of sandy shoreline, its shallow depth and calm waves make it a popular family beach destination. The stunning West Coast sunsets here are a spectacle unique to the region.
chungcheong-007.emotionalDescription: Mallipo is a place to feel the romance of the West Coast. Leisurely enjoying the beach and watching the red sunset in the evening brings true healing. Taean's pristine sea washes away the fatigue of everyday life.

chungcheong-008.name: Anmyeondo Island, Taean
chungcheong-008.summary: A flower-lover's island famous for tulips and red spider lilies — Taean's crown jewel
chungcheong-008.historicalDescription: Anmyeondo Island is located at the tip of the Taean Peninsula and was connected to the mainland in the 1970s. It is home to a red spider lily park, tulip park, and natural recreation forest, making it a famous nature tourism destination. The autumn red spider lily festival is particularly famous nationwide.
chungcheong-008.emotionalDescription: Anmyeondo is a place where a parade of flowers unfolds in every season. Walking through the spring tulip fields and the autumn red spider lily fields and marveling at the beauty of nature, strolling along the coastline lets you feel the spirit of the West Coast. It offers precious time to commune with nature.

chungcheong-009.name: Seosan Rock-carved Buddhist Triad
chungcheong-009.summary: National Treasure No. 84 — an enormous Goryeo-era rock-carved Buddhist triad famous for its serene smile
chungcheong-009.historicalDescription: The Seosan Maae Samjonbul are rock-carved Buddhist figures created during the Goryeo era, consisting of a central Buddha flanked by two bodhisattvas. Carved into a cliff face at 9m height, they were designated National Treasure No. 84 in 1963. They represent Buddhist culture across the West Coast region.
chungcheong-009.emotionalDescription: The rock-carved Buddhist triad is a magnificent work of faith carved into stone. Looking up at the great figures and marveling at the dedication of Goryeo artisans, you can feel peace from the serene smiles of the figures. It is a place where the deep-rooted faith of the West Coast can be felt.

chungcheong-010.name: Hapdeok Cathedral, Seosan
chungcheong-010.summary: Korea's first Western-style cathedral — a stunning example of rural Gothic architecture
chungcheong-010.historicalDescription: Hapdeok Cathedral was completed in 1932 as Korea's first Western-style cathedral. Built with the voluntary donations of Catholic faithful, it showcases pure Gothic architectural beauty. It was designated a National Folk Cultural Heritage in 1991.
chungcheong-010.emotionalDescription: Hapdeok Cathedral is an architectural work of art born from the passion of faith. Admiring the beauty of Gothic architecture and the brilliance of the stained glass, you can feel the devotion of the martyrs. The charm of a countryside cathedral is uniquely captivating.

chungcheong-011.name: Janghang Station, Seocheon
chungcheong-011.summary: A retro heritage rail station turned vintage tourism attraction, famous as a drama filming location
chungcheong-011.historicalDescription: Janghang Station opened in 1930 and was destroyed in the Korean War but later restored. It gained fame as a filming location for the KBS drama 'Janghang Train,' transforming into a retro tourism destination. The restored station building and a steam locomotive are on display.
chungcheong-011.emotionalDescription: Janghang Station is a retro space where time seems to have stopped. Feeling the atmosphere of the old station and taking photos with the steam locomotive as a backdrop, you can create lasting memories. It is a place to experience the charm of modern cultural heritage.

chungcheong-012.name: Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
chungcheong-012.summary: The landmark temple of Songnisan, a UNESCO-designated mountain sanctuary with millennium-old history
chungcheong-012.historicalDescription: Beopjusa Temple was founded in 553 CE by Monk Uisindaedeok and is located within Songnisan National Park. It stored the Tripitaka Koreana during the Goryeo era, and holds many treasures including the Palsangjeon (National Treasure No. 55) and a stone seated Buddha. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
chungcheong-012.emotionalDescription: Beopjusa is a thousand-year-old temple blessed by the spiritual energy of Songnisan. Within the atmosphere of venerable halls and surrounding nature in harmony, you can find peace of mind. The beauty of the Palsangjeon in particular is a sight to behold.

chungcheong-013.name: Munjangdae Peak, Songnisan
chungcheong-013.summary: The summit of Songnisan — a hiker's ultimate reward with panoramic views across rolling green mountains
chungcheong-013.historicalDescription: Munjangdae is the highest peak of Songnisan at 1,057m elevation. Its name comes from the rock face resembling the character for 'writing' (文). As the highest peak of Songnisan National Park, the views from the summit are extraordinary. The national park was designated in 1984.
chungcheong-013.emotionalDescription: Munjangdae is the ultimate goal of hiking Songnisan. The sense of achievement upon reaching the summit after a demanding trail, and the view of the endless blue mountains from the top, are unforgettable experiences. It is a moment of being overwhelmed by the pure majesty of nature.

chungcheong-014.name: Expo Science Park, Daejeon
chungcheong-014.summary: Legacy of Daejeon's 1993 World's Fair — a science-themed park and beloved city landmark
chungcheong-014.historicalDescription: Expo Science Park was established for the 1993 Daejeon World Expo. It features Hanbit Tower, Expo Bridge, and the Daejeon Arts Center, and is equipped with a science museum and advanced technology exhibits. It has become an iconic park and landmark of Daejeon.
chungcheong-014.emotionalDescription: Expo Science Park is a space where science and art meet. Surveying downtown Daejeon from Hanbit Tower and satisfying curiosity at the science museum through various hands-on activities — the beautiful night lighting makes it a pleasant urban retreat.

chungcheong-015.name: Hanbat Arboretum, Daejeon
chungcheong-015.summary: Daejeon's cherished arboretum, loved for its 23 themed gardens and tranquil walking paths
chungcheong-015.historicalDescription: Hanbat Arboretum was established in 1993 to commemorate the World Expo. It displays over 1,100 plant species across 23 themed gardens, and is beloved by Daejeon citizens as a recreational space. Beautiful flowers of different varieties bloom throughout the four seasons.
chungcheong-015.emotionalDescription: Hanbat Arboretum is Daejeon citizens' garden. Strolling through themed gardens to admire seasonal flowers and trees, and walking quiet paths to feel nature in the heart of the city — it is a great spot to spend a relaxed time with family.

chungcheong-016.name: Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest, Daejeon
chungcheong-016.summary: A cypress forest retreat near Daejeon, popular for phytoncide-rich woodland walks and family camping
chungcheong-016.historicalDescription: Jangtaesan Natural Recreation Forest was established in 1986. It features a well-developed cypress forest where you can enjoy the benefits of phytoncides. Hiking trails, campsites, and outdoor education facilities make it a popular family retreat destination.
chungcheong-016.emotionalDescription: Jangtaesan is a healing space filled with the fragrance of cypress trees. Walking through the forest and breathing in phytoncides and fresh air melts away stress. It offers precious time to commune with nature and escape the hustle of city life.

chungcheong-017.name: Sangdangsanseong Fortress, Cheongju
chungcheong-017.summary: A Baekje-era mountain fortress above Cheongju, combining history and panoramic city views
chungcheong-017.historicalDescription: Sangdangsanseong is a mountain fortress built during the Baekje era, located on Sangdangsan, the guardian mountain of Cheongju. The 4km-circumference walls remain, and it was designated a Historic Site in 1970. Its position overlooking downtown Cheongju provides excellent panoramic views.
chungcheong-017.emotionalDescription: Sangdangsanseong is a mountain fortress that holds the history of Cheongju. Walking along the walls and imagining the Baekje era, the view of downtown Cheongju from the summit gives a satisfying sense of achievement. It is a historic walking course easily accessible from downtown.

chungcheong-018.name: Cheongju National Museum
chungcheong-018.summary: The central museum of the Chungcheong region, housing an impressive collection of Baekje and beyond
chungcheong-018.historicalDescription: Cheongju National Museum opened in 1969 as a national museum. It exhibits the history and culture of the Chungcheong region, centered on Baekje, Goryeo, and Joseon era artifacts. It holds National Treasure-level items including the Gilt-bronze Incense Burner.
chungcheong-018.emotionalDescription: Cheongju National Museum is a place where you can take in the history of Chungcheong at a glance. Through diverse artifacts you can understand Baekje culture and Joseon-era lifestyles, and in the quiet exhibition space you can think deeply about history.

chungcheong-019.name: Sejong Lake Park
chungcheong-019.summary: The signature park of Sejong City, renowned for its lakeside promenade and beautiful evening lights
chungcheong-019.historicalDescription: Sejong Lake Park was created alongside the establishment of Sejong Special Autonomous City. Opened in 2011, its lakeside promenade and night scenery are popular. It has become the signature recreational space of Sejong City.
chungcheong-019.emotionalDescription: Sejong Lake Park is the pride of Sejong City. Strolling along the lakeside and feeling the leisurely pace of the new city, you can admire the beautiful night view of the lake illuminated by evening lights. It is a daily retreat for Sejong residents.

jeolla-001.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
jeolla-001.summary: Korea's largest traditional hanok village — the living heart of Korean culinary and architectural heritage
jeolla-001.historicalDescription: Jeonju Hanok Village has been a concentrated area of hanok houses since the 1910s. Over 800 hanok homes are preserved, with designated hanok clusters protecting traditional architecture. Historic sites including Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Omokdae, and Hyanggyo are here, and traditional crafts and food culture have flourished.
jeolla-001.emotionalDescription: Jeonju Hanok Village is a living museum of Korean tradition. Walking along the curved rooftiles and stone-walled alleys gives you a taste of Joseon-era spirit, and strolling the lanes in hanbok you feel as if you are time-traveling to the past. The taste of bibimbap and makgeolli are memories that never fade.

jeolla-002.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeonju
jeolla-002.summary: The royal shrine enshrining King Taejo Yi Seonggye's portrait — a powerful symbol of the Joseon founding
jeolla-002.historicalDescription: Gyeonggijeon was built in 1410 to enshrine the portrait of King Taejo Yi Seonggye. As the ancestral seat of the Jeonju Yi clan, it was modeled after Gyeongbokgung's Geunjeongjeon hall. Restored in 1971, it is an important historic site showcasing the founding history of the Joseon Dynasty.
jeolla-002.emotionalDescription: Gyeonggijeon is a place that symbolizes the beginning of 500 years of Joseon history. Viewing the portrait of King Taejo and reflecting on the founding of Joseon, you can feel the dignity of the ancestral seat of the Jeonju Yi clan. It is a place within Hanok Village where you can physically sense the weight of history.

jeolla-003.name: Naganeupseong Fortress Village, Suncheon
jeolla-003.summary: A living Joseon-era walled town where residents still dwell — Korea's finest open-air folk museum
jeolla-003.historicalDescription: Naganeupseong Fortress Village was built during the Joseon era of King Taejo in 1397.
