Over 300 households still live there today maintaining traditional lifestyles, earning it the name 'living folk museum.' Designated Folk Cultural Heritage No. 302 in 1983, the traditional houses and fortress walls are well preserved.
jeolla-003.emotionalDescription: Naganeupseong is a traditional village where time seems to have stopped. Seeing the lives of people living within the fortress walls gives you a sense of Korean traditional village life. Stay overnight in a guesthouse and immerse yourself fully in the scent of tradition.

jeolla-004.name: Suncheonman Bay Wetland
jeolla-004.summary: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve where sweeping reed beds and migratory birds create a living masterpiece
jeolla-004.historicalDescription: Suncheonman Bay Wetland was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2003, and in 2006 was designated a Natural Monument by the Korean government. It is an important wetland visited by over 140 species of migratory birds, and the autumn reed beds are a spectacular sight.
jeolla-004.emotionalDescription: Suncheonman Bay is the finest work of art bestowed by nature. Walking among the reed beds and admiring the waves of reeds swaying in the breeze, the wetland scenery at sunset draws gasps of admiration. It is a place where you can feel the cycle of nature and the preciousness of life.

jeolla-005.name: Hyangil-am Hermitage, Yeosu
jeolla-005.summary: A cliff-top sea hermitage in Yeosu, renowned as one of Korea's finest sunrise destinations
jeolla-005.historicalDescription: Hyangil-am was founded in 644 CE by Monk Wonhyo, perched on a seaside cliff. Its name means 'facing the sunrise,' and it is renowned as one of Korea's finest sunrise spots. It was selected as one of the top 10 sunrise spots in Korea in 1992.
jeolla-005.emotionalDescription: Hyangil-am is a hermitage that embraces the sea. The sunrise viewed from the cliff is a grand spectacle, and meditating to the sound of temple bells reverberating over the sea is a special experience. It is a sacred space where mountain, sea, and Buddhism become one.

jeolla-006.name: Odongdo Island, Yeosu
jeolla-006.summary: The 'Camellia Island' of Yeosu — a beloved seaside park where winter blossoms dazzle visitors
jeolla-006.historicalDescription: Odongdo Island was developed as a park in 1962 in the waters off Yeosu. Its name derives from the paulownia trees that once grew there, but it is actually famous for its many camellia trees, earning the nickname 'Camellia Island.' It was designated a National Folk Cultural Heritage in 1972.
jeolla-006.emotionalDescription: Odongdo is an island filled with the fragrance of camellia blossoms. Walking through the camellia tunnel while breathing in the sea breeze and floral scent, the romantic sea scenery accompanied by the musical fountain is enchanting. It is a beautiful island representing the sea of Yeosu.

jeolla-007.name: Yeosu Maritime Cable Car
jeolla-007.summary: Korea's first sea cable car — a romantic way to experience the legendary night sea of Yeosu
jeolla-007.historicalDescription: The Yeosu Maritime Cable Car, opened in 2014, is Korea's first sea cable car. It operates over a 1.5km stretch between Dolsan and Jasando Island, and a crystal-floor cruise gondola is also offered. It has established itself as a new landmark of Yeosu.
jeolla-007.emotionalDescription: The Yeosu Maritime Cable Car is a romantic way to enjoy Yeosu's famous night sea. Crossing over the water and taking in the night view of Yeosu is fantastic, and looking down at the sea through the transparent floor is an unforgettable thrill.

jeolla-008.name: Soswaewon Garden, Damyang
jeolla-008.summary: Korea's finest Joseon-era private garden — a serene retreat embodying the scholar's ideal of natural harmony
jeolla-008.historicalDescription: Soswaewon Garden was created in the 1560s by Yang San-bo during the Joseon middle period. The name 'Soswae' means leisurely enjoyment, reflecting the garden philosophy of Joseon literati. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009.
jeolla-008.emotionalDescription: Soswaewon is a space where you can feel the leisurely ease of a Joseon literati. Strolling through a garden that achieves harmony between nature as it is and human artistry, you can imagine the unhurried life of scholars of old. It is a place that shows the very essence of Eastern garden aesthetics.

jeolla-009.name: Juknokwon Bamboo Garden, Damyang
jeolla-009.summary: A famous bamboo ecological park renowned for its peaceful walking paths through towering green groves
jeolla-009.historicalDescription: Juknokwon is a bamboo ecological park established in 2003. Eight varieties of bamboo are planted here with approximately 2km of walking paths laid out through them. It was selected as Asia's first World Class Forest in 2012.
jeolla-009.emotionalDescription: Juknokwon is a place to heal in the tranquility of bamboo. The sunlight filtering through the stalks, the sound of the wind, and the hushing rustle of the bamboo provide nature's own ASMR. Walking the paths, you can find profound peace of mind.

jeolla-010.name: Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
jeolla-010.summary: A 1,400-year-old temple in Seonunsan, famed for its breathtaking winter-to-spring camellia blooms
jeolla-010.historicalDescription: Seonunsa Temple was founded in 577 CE and has 1,400 years of history. Located at the foot of Seonunsan Mountain, the camellia trees surrounding the temple are famous. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List together with other Gochang historic sites in 2009.
jeolla-010.emotionalDescription: Seonunsa is a beautiful temple adorned with camellia blossoms. The sight of brilliant red camellias in full bloom as winter turns to spring is spectacular, and within the quietude of this millennium-old temple you can purify your heart.

jeolla-011.name: Gochang Eupseong Fortress
jeolla-011.summary: A Joseon-era walled town and UNESCO World Heritage Site — the crown jewel of Gochang's history
jeolla-011.historicalDescription: Gochang Eupseong was built during the reign of King Sejong in 1416. The 1.6km earthen walls remain, and in 2009 the Gochang Historic Districts were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The traditional homes within the fortress walls add to its historic value.
jeolla-011.emotionalDescription: Gochang Eupseong is a place where the charm of the Joseon era is alive. Walking along the fortress walls and imagining the old walled town's appearance, and feeling the atmosphere of the quiet alleyways, you can experience the UNESCO World Heritage history of Gochang.

jeolla-012.name: Gwanghallu Garden, Namwon
jeolla-012.summary: The garden setting of Korea's most beloved love story, Chunhyangjeon — pavilions, ponds, and romance
jeolla-012.historicalDescription: Gwanghallu Garden is a Joseon-era pavilion and garden complex that became the setting of the classic tale Chunhyangjeon. Built in 1419, it features Gwanghallu Pavilion harmonized with a beautiful lotus pond. It was designated a Scenic Site in 1968.
jeolla-012.emotionalDescription: Gwanghallu Garden is imbued with the love of Chunhyang and Yi Mongnyong. Walking across the bridge spanning the pond and recalling a scene from Chunhyangjeon, you can feel the romance of Korean tradition in this beautiful garden. It is Namwon's most representative cultural heritage.

jeolla-013.name: Chunhyang Theme Park, Namwon
jeolla-013.summary: A theme park celebrating the classic tale Chunhyangjeon — an immersive traditional culture experience
jeolla-013.historicalDescription: Chunhyang Theme Park is a theme park centered on Chunhyangjeon, opened in 2001. It recreates the setting of the story and runs various programs including hanbok experience and traditional wedding ceremonies. The annual Chunhyang Festival promotes traditional culture nationwide.
jeolla-013.emotionalDescription: Chunhyang Theme Park is a place that guides you into the world of Chunhyangjeon. Viewing the traditional houses and facilities to feel the Joseon atmosphere, and taking photos in hanbok, you can create special memories. It is a wonderful place to lightly experience Korean traditional culture.

jeolla-014.name: Gunsan Modern History Cultural District
jeolla-014.summary: A preserved colonial-era streetscape where the pain and culture of Korea's modern history come alive
jeolla-014.historicalDescription: Gunsan's Modern History Cultural District was designated a national cultural heritage site in 2011. Colonial-era modern buildings including Chodwon Photo Studio, Gunsan Customs House, and Gunsan Iron Bridge are preserved. It faithfully retains the appearance of 1930s Gunsan.
jeolla-014.emotionalDescription: Gunsan's Modern History Cultural District is a place to feel the painful history and culture of the modern era. Taking photos at Chodwon Photo Studio and walking among the old buildings, you can imagine the appearance of colonial Gunsan. The atmosphere of faded signs and old alleyways is uniquely captivating.

jeolla-015.name: Chodwon Photo Studio, Gunsan
jeolla-015.summary: Opened in 1939 — Korea's oldest continuously operating photo studio and a beloved modern cultural heritage
jeolla-015.historicalDescription: Chodwon Photo Studio opened in 1939 and remains in operation, making it the oldest photography studio still operating in Korea. Its original appearance is fully preserved, giving it great value as a modern cultural heritage. It is also famous as a filming location for dramas and films.
jeolla-015.emotionalDescription: Chodwon Photo Studio is a space where time seems to have stopped. You can fully feel the atmosphere of the 1930s and experience the sensibility of the modern era by having black-and-white portraits taken. It is a symbolic space of Gunsan's modern culture.

jeolla-016.name: Seonyudo Island, Gunsan
jeolla-016.summary: A beautiful island off Gunsan coast, famous for its pebble beaches and spectacular West Coast sunsets
jeolla-016.historicalDescription: Seonyudo is an island in the waters off Gunsan, connected to the mainland by a bridge in the 1970s. The pebble beach and sunsets are famous, and it has developed considerably as a tourist destination in recent years.
jeolla-016.emotionalDescription: Seonyudo is an island where you can feel the romance of the West Coast. Strolling the pebble beach and admiring the sunset, and enjoying the quiet fishing village atmosphere — the combination of the West Coast's tidal flats and golden sunset is truly spectacular.

jeolla-017.name: Mireuksa Temple Site, Iksan
jeolla-017.summary: The site of Baekje's greatest temple, where a UNESCO-listed stone pagoda and golden reliquary were unearthed
jeolla-017.historicalDescription: Mireuksa Temple Site is the location of the largest Baekje-era temple, founded in 602 CE. A stone pagoda and golden reliquary were excavated and the stone pagoda was designated a National Treasure in 1997. In 2015 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Baekje Historic Districts.
jeolla-017.emotionalDescription: Mireuksa Temple Site was once the center of Baekje Buddhism. Viewing the restored stone pagoda and imagining Baekje's prosperity, and glimpsing the culture of the time through the excavated artifacts, it is a place that lets you feel the great depth of history.

jeolla-018.name: Wanggung-ri Historic Site, Iksan
jeolla-018.summary: A UNESCO-listed Baekje royal palace site — a rare window into Baekje's regal life and grandeur
jeolla-018.historicalDescription: Wanggung-ri Historic Site is the location of a Baekje-era royal palace, where archaeological excavations began in the 1990s. Large building foundations and stone artifacts were unearthed, and in 2015 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Baekje Historic Districts.
jeolla-018.emotionalDescription: Wanggung-ri is the site where the Baekje palace once stood. Viewing the excavated grounds and imagining the lives of Baekje kings, and understanding the culture of the time through the exhibited artifacts, it is a place that reveals an important chapter of Korean history.

jeolla-019.name: Naejangsan Mountain, Jeongeup
jeolla-019.summary: Honam's foremost autumn foliage destination — Naejangsan National Park ablaze with color every fall
jeolla-019.historicalDescription: Naejangsan was designated a national park in 1971 and is famous as the premier autumn foliage destination in the Honam (Jeolla) region. The scenery of temple clusters centered around Naejangsa Temple combined with autumn foliage is spectacular. The 763m mountain is also popular for hiking.
jeolla-019.emotionalDescription: Naejangsan is a mountain famous for its blazing red autumn foliage. Walking through the foliage tunnel and savoring the season to the full, and purifying your mind in the quietude of Naejangsa Temple — you will instantly understand why it is called Honam's finest autumn foliage spot.

jeolla-020.name: Godu Museum, Jeongeup
jeolla-020.summary: A museum commemorating former President Park Chung-hee, offering a window into Korea's modern history
jeolla-020.historicalDescription: Godu Museum is a museum commemorating former President Park Chung-hee, opened in 1999. It exhibits Park Chung-hee's life and achievements. Jeongeup is also the hometown of Yuk Young-su, the wife of the former president.
jeolla-020.emotionalDescription: Godu Museum is a place that shows a chapter of Korea's modern history. Understanding the process of Korea's modernization through the life of former President Park Chung-hee, it invites you to think about various perspectives on historical figures.

jeolla-021.name: Yudalsan Mountain, Mokpo
jeolla-021.summary: Mokpo's guardian mountain commanding sweeping views of the harbor and the Dadohae archipelago
jeolla-021.historicalDescription: Yudalsan is Mokpo's guardian mountain at 228m elevation. It commands an excellent view of Mokpo Port and the Yeongsan River estuary, and has historical significance as an area with deep colonial-era roots. It is an essential part of Mokpo's skyline and identity.
jeolla-021.emotionalDescription: Yudalsan is a place where you can see the full panorama of Mokpo at a glance. Climbing the hiking trail and admiring the scenery of Mokpo Port and the Dadohae archipelago, the view at sunset becomes an unforgettable memory. It is an essential stop on any Mokpo trip.

jeolla-022.name: Mokpo Modern History Museum
jeolla-022.summary: A museum tracing Mokpo's modern history — from the port-opening era through the independence movement
jeolla-022.historicalDescription: Mokpo Modern History Museum opened in 2011 and exhibits the history of Mokpo's port-opening and modern era. It shows the appearance of colonial-era Mokpo and the history of the independence movement, introducing Mokpo's modern cultural heritage to visitors.
jeolla-022.emotionalDescription: The Modern History Museum is a place to understand Mokpo's modern history. Viewing the appearance of Mokpo during the port-opening era and the history of the anti-Japanese independence movement, you can feel the lives of the people of Mokpo. It is an educational space that deepens understanding of a Mokpo trip.

jeolla-023.name: May 18th Memorial Park, Gwangju
jeolla-023.summary: A park commemorating the May 18th Democratization Movement — a sacred site of Korean democracy
jeolla-023.historicalDescription: May 18th Memorial Park was established on the grounds of the former South Jeolla Provincial Office, which was the headquarters of the martial law command during the May 18th Democratization Movement of 1980. Created as a park in 1997, it is a space for commemorating the victims of the democratization movement.
jeolla-023.emotionalDescription: May 18th Memorial Park is a sacred space that honors those who gave their lives for democracy. Paying tribute to the victims at the memorial and reflecting on the preciousness of democracy, it is a place that makes you deeply feel a painful page of Korea's modern history.

jeolla-024.name: Mudeungsan Mountain, Gwangju
jeolla-024.summary: Gwangju's guardian mountain, renowned for its dramatic rocky ridges, mountain temples, and panoramic views
jeolla-024.historicalDescription: Mudeungsan is Gwangju's guardian mountain at 1,187m elevation. Designated a provincial park in 1972, it is characterized by its rocky ridgeline near the summit. There are temples including Wonhyosa and Jeungsimsa, and it is popular with hikers from across the region.
jeolla-024.emotionalDescription: Mudeungsan is the retreat and pride of Gwangju's citizens. Hiking along the rocky ridgeline and feeling the thrill, and viewing the panorama of Gwangju from the summit makes it all worthwhile. It is a place where the tranquility of the temples and the grandeur of the mountain come together beautifully.

jeolla-025.name: National Asian Culture Complex (ACC), Gwangju
jeolla-025.summary: The hub of Asian cultural exchange — Gwangju's striking modern landmark for art and performance
jeolla-025.historicalDescription: The National Asian Culture Complex opened in 2015 as a cultural complex. Designated as the ACC in 2012, it serves as the center for Asian cultural exchange. It is a modern architectural structure featuring exhibition halls, performance venues, and a library.
jeolla-025.emotionalDescription: The Asian Culture Complex is a space to experience Asian culture. Through diverse exhibitions and performances you can encounter the varied cultures of Asia, and the modern architecture itself is a striking sight to behold. It is Gwangju's landmark of contemporary culture.

gyeongsang-001.name: Bulguksa Temple, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-001.summary: The pinnacle of Silla Buddhist art — a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site of extraordinary beauty
gyeongsang-001.historicalDescription: Bulguksa Temple was founded in 528 CE during the reign of King Beopheung of Silla and is regarded as the highest achievement of Silla Buddhist art. The Dabotap and Seokgatap pagodas are famous, and it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 1995. There are many National Treasure-grade structures including Geungnakjeon, Yeonhwagyo Bridge, and Cheongunggyo Bridge.
gyeongsang-001.emotionalDescription: Bulguksa is a space that symbolizes the golden age of Silla. Standing before Dabotap and Seokgatap, you feel the devotion of the Silla people and their passion for Buddhism, and the scenery harmonized with the beautiful nature of Tohamsan foothills is spectacular. You can experience the very essence of Korean Buddhist culture.

gyeongsang-002.name: Seokguram Grotto, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-002.summary: The masterwork of Silla sculpture — the supreme achievement of East Asian Buddhist art
gyeongsang-002.historicalDescription: Seokguram is an artificial stone cave temple founded in 751 CE by Kim Dae-seong. Around the central main Buddha figure, statues of bodhisattvas, heavenly kings, and the four guardian kings are harmoniously arranged. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List together with Bulguksa in 1995.
gyeongsang-002.emotionalDescription: Seokguram is the supreme achievement of East Asian Buddhist art. Entering the stone grotto, you feel the hidden devotion of Silla sculptors, and the smile of the main Buddha figure brings peace to all who behold it. The mysterious atmosphere of the sculptures illuminated by gentle lighting is an unforgettable experience.

gyeongsang-003.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-003.summary: Silla royalty's resting place — a vast burial mound park including the famous Cheonmachong tomb
gyeongsang-003.historicalDescription: Daereungwon is an area where the burial mounds of Silla-era royals and aristocrats are concentrated. It contains numerous tombs including Cheonmachong, Geumnyeongchong, and Eunmyo, and was designated a Historic Site in 1973. Located in the center of Gyeongju, it is easily accessible.
gyeongsang-003.emotionalDescription: Daereungwon is where the history of Silla lies at rest. Walking among the landscape-like burial mounds and imagining the lives of Silla royals, and feeling the splendor of Silla culture through the artifacts excavated from Cheonmachong — at night, lights illuminate the burial mounds creating a mysterious atmosphere.

gyeongsang-004.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-004.summary: Asia's oldest surviving astronomical observatory — a Silla-era National Treasure and icon of ancient science
gyeongsang-004.historicalDescription: Cheomseongdae is an astronomical observatory built during the reign of Queen Seondeok of Silla, designated National Treasure No. 31 in 1962. The cylindrical stone structure was used for astronomical observation at the time. It is known as the oldest astronomical observatory in Asia.
gyeongsang-004.emotionalDescription: Cheomseongdae is a relic that symbolizes Silla's love of astronomy. Looking at Cheomseongdae near Wolji Pond, you feel the curiosity and wisdom of the Silla people about the universe. Cheomseongdae silhouetted against a night sky full of stars is a fantastical sight.

gyeongsang-005.name: Hwangnyongsa Temple Site, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-005.summary: The ruins of Silla's greatest temple, once home to the legendary nine-story wooden pagoda
gyeongsang-005.historicalDescription: Hwangnyongsa Temple Site is the location of Hwangnyongsa, the largest temple of the Silla era. Founded in 645 CE during the reign of Queen Seondeok, it was famous for its nine-story wooden pagoda. Currently only the stone pagoda and flagpole supports remain. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 2000.
gyeongsang-005.emotionalDescription: Hwangnyongsa Temple Site is a place where you can feel the former might of Silla's greatest temple. Through the remaining artifacts, you can imagine the scale of the temple and sense the ambition of Queen Seondeok. It is a site of deep significance as a historical center of Silla.

gyeongsang-006.name: Yangdong Village, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-006.summary: One of Korea's oldest traditional villages — a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage living museum of aristocratic life
gyeongsang-006.historicalDescription: Yangdong Village is the oldest traditional village in Gyeongju, where the Wolseong Son clan and Yeogang Yi clan have lived for over 500 years. Joseon-era aristocratic houses and traditional customs are well preserved, and it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 2010.
gyeongsang-006.emotionalDescription: Yangdong Village is a treasury of living Korean traditional culture. Viewing the aristocratic houses preserved in every alley and imagining Joseon-era life, and feeling the warmth of Korean tradition through interaction with village residents — it is a living scene of intangible cultural heritage.

gyeongsang-007.name: Bunhwangsa Temple, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-007.summary: A Silla-era temple with Korea's oldest and most distinctive modular brick pagoda — National Treasure No. 30
gyeongsang-007.historicalDescription: Bunhwangsa Temple was founded in 634 CE during the reign of Queen Seondeok. It is famous for its modular brick pagoda (moyeon stone pagoda), and also has a stone seated Buddha. Designated a National Treasure in 1962, it is an important site showcasing Silla Buddhist culture.
gyeongsang-007.emotionalDescription: Bunhwangsa is a temple that shows a chapter of Silla Buddhist culture. Viewing the uniquely shaped modular brick pagoda and feeling the architectural beauty of the Silla people, you can purify your mind within the quiet temple atmosphere.

gyeongsang-008.name: Hahoe Village, Andong
gyeongsang-008.summary: The foremost Joseon-era aristocratic village — a UNESCO World Heritage gem and birthplace of the Hahoe mask
gyeongsang-008.historicalDescription: Hahoe Village has been a representative Joseon-era aristocratic village since the 16th century. The Pungsan Ryu clan has lived here for over 600 years, and it is also famous as the birthplace of the Hahoe mask. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 2010.
gyeongsang-008.emotionalDescription: Hahoe Village is a living museum of Joseon aristocratic culture. Viewing the traditional homes set on geomantically auspicious land where the Nakdonggang River curves around, you can feel the lives of Joseon aristocrats. The mysterious atmosphere of the Hahoe Byeolshin Gut Mask Play offers a truly special experience.

gyeongsang-009.name: Byeongsan Seowon, Andong
gyeongsang-009.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Confucian academy set against the Nakdonggang River's breathtaking scenery
gyeongsang-009.historicalDescription: Byeongsan Seowon was built in 1572 to honor Neo-Confucian scholar Toegye Yi Hwang. Mandaeru Pavilion is its most famous feature, and in 2019 it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of the Korean Seowon. The academy is set against the spectacular scenery of the Nakdonggang River.
gyeongsang-009.emotionalDescription: Byeongsan Seowon is a place where the scholarship and spirit of Toegye Yi Hwang still lives. The view of the Nakdonggang River from Mandaeru Pavilion evokes the yearning of Joseon scholars, and in the quiet academy you can experience the spirit of Confucian learning.

gyeongsang-010.name: Dosan Seowon, Andong
gyeongsang-010.summary: Where Toegye Yi Hwang taught — the spiritual heartland of Joseon Neo-Confucianism
gyeongsang-010.historicalDescription: Dosan Seowon was built in 1574 at the site where Toegye Yi Hwang lectured. It was created to honor Toegye's scholarship and virtue, and was designated a Historic Site in 1969. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2019.
gyeongsang-010.emotionalDescription: Dosan Seowon is a sacred space where you can feel the footsteps of Toegye Yi Hwang. Savoring Toegye's poetry and scholarship while gazing at the scenery of Dosan from the academy, you can experience the very essence of Joseon Confucianism.

gyeongsang-011.name: Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
gyeongsang-011.summary: Daegu's foremost temple on Palgongsan — a 1,500-year-old spiritual sanctuary of deep history
gyeongsang-011.historicalDescription: Donghwasa Temple was founded in 493 CE by Monk Yeongi and is a thousand-year-old temple with 1,500 years of history. Located on Palgongsan, it is famous as the place where King Sejo sought to reclaim his throne. It underwent large-scale restoration in the 1990s.
gyeongsang-011.emotionalDescription: Donghwasa is Daegu's representative temple, blessed by the spiritual energy of Palgongsan. Within the atmosphere of its grand scale and beautiful halls harmonized with the surrounding nature, you can find peace of mind. It is a place where you can feel the faith of Daegu's citizens.

gyeongsang-012.name: Palgongsan Mountain, Daegu
gyeongsang-012.summary: Daegu's guardian mountain — a hiker's paradise of ancient temples, clear streams, and seasonal beauty
gyeongsang-012.historicalDescription: Palgongsan is Daegu's guardian mountain at 1,193m elevation. Designated a provincial park in 1976, it is home to many famous temples including Donghwasa, Pagaesa, and Buinsa. The valleys and walking paths are well developed, making it a favorite retreat for citizens.
gyeongsang-012.emotionalDescription: Palgongsan is the retreat and spiritual mountain of Daegu's citizens. Visiting temples and meditating, and climbing along hiking trails to view the Daegu cityscape from the summit makes it all worthwhile. It is a mountain that shows entirely different charms in all four seasons.

gyeongsang-013.name: Apsan Mountain, Daegu
gyeongsang-013.summary: Daegu's urban mountain overlooking the city, known for its cable car and breathtaking night views
gyeongsang-013.historicalDescription: Apsan is a mountain located to the south of downtown Daegu at 660m elevation. Designated a city natural park in 1981, it features an observation deck and cable car for overlooking the Daegu cityscape. Hiking trails and walking paths are well developed.
gyeongsang-013.emotionalDescription: Apsan is a place where you can see downtown Daegu at a glance. Riding the cable car up or walking along the hiking trails, you can enjoy the city and nature simultaneously. The glittering night view of downtown Daegu is an unforgettable scene.

gyeongsang-014.name: Kim Gwang-seok Street, Daegu
gyeongsang-014.summary: A mural alley honoring the beloved late singer Kim Gwang-seok — Daegu's most soulful cultural landmark
gyeongsang-014.historicalDescription: Kim Gwang-seok Street is a mural street developed in the 2010s as a space honoring Daegu-born singer Kim Gwang-seok. Various murals line the alleyways near Bangcheon Market, with sculptures and installations referencing his song lyrics.
gyeongsang-014.emotionalDescription: Kim Gwang-seok Street is a place where nostalgia and emotion coexist. Walking through alleys full of murals and graffiti while recalling Kim Gwang-seok's songs, you can feel the passion of young artists. It is Daegu's new beloved cultural destination.

gyeongsang-015.name: Buseoksa Temple, Yeongju
gyeongsang-015.summary: A national treasure among treasures — home of Korea's oldest surviving wooden hall, the Muryangsujeon
gyeongsang-015.historicalDescription: Buseoksa Temple was founded in 676 CE by Monk Euisindaedeok, with its Muryangsujeon (National Treasure No. 18), built in 1376, being one of Korea's oldest surviving wooden structures. It received royal patronage from several Joseon kings and occupies an important place in Korean architectural history.
gyeongsang-015.emotionalDescription: Buseoksa is a place that shows the essence of Korean traditional architecture. Looking at the national treasure Muryangsujeon and marveling at the beauty of Goryeo-era architecture, you can purify your mind within the atmosphere of the temple harmonized with the surrounding nature.

gyeongsang-016.name: Sosu Seowon, Yeongju
gyeongsang-016.summary: Korea's very first Confucian academy — a UNESCO World Heritage Site of supreme historical importance
gyeongsang-016.historicalDescription: Sosu Seowon was established in 1542 as Korea's first Confucian academy, built to honor An Hyang. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of the Korean Seowon in 2019. Its name 'Sosu' (韶灘) means 'beautiful waterside.'
gyeongsang-016.emotionalDescription: Sosu Seowon is a place that symbolizes the very beginning of Korean Confucian academies. Feeling the history of education and scholarship in Korea's very first academy, and gazing at the scenery of the academy harmonized with beautiful nature, you can sense the yearning of Joseon scholars.

gyeongsang-017.name: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-017.summary: A Silla crown prince's secondary palace and garden — Gyeongju's most enchanting night view
gyeongsang-017.historicalDescription: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond (formerly known as Anapji) was the secondary palace of the Silla royal family. Created in 674 CE during the reign of King Munmu, only the pond and pavilion foundations remain today. Designated a Historical Monument in 1979, it is famous for its breathtaking night scenery.
gyeongsang-017.emotionalDescription: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond is where the Silla royal palace once stood. The night view of the illuminated pond evokes imagination of Silla's splendor and presents the beautiful scenery that represents Gyeongju at night. It is a place imbued with the dreams and romance of Silla.

gyeongsang-018.name: Gyochon Village, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-018.summary: Gyeongju's oldest village — a hanok heritage district where Silla history and tradition still breathe
gyeongsang-018.historicalDescription: Gyochon Village is the oldest village in Gyeongju, formed since the 1350s. The Gyeongju Choi clan and Gangneung Kim clan maintain traditions here, and it has been developed as Gyeongju Gyochon Hanok Village.
gyeongsang-018.emotionalDescription: Gyochon Village is where the history of Gyeongju began. Walking the traditional hanok streets and alleyways and feeling the tranquil atmosphere of Gyeongju, you can experience the spirit of Silla through a hanbok experience. It is a hidden gem of a Gyeongju travel spot.

gyeongsang-019.name: Hansando Island, Tongyeong
gyeongsang-019.summary: The site of the Battle of Hansando — where Admiral Yi Sun-sin's brilliant strategy turned the tide of war
gyeongsang-019.historicalDescription: Hansando Island is where the Battle of Hansando took place in 1592, a historic site where Admiral Yi Sun-sin's military strategy shone brilliantly. It has the Hansando Battle Memorial Park and a statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, and has developed into a popular tourist destination.
gyeongsang-019.emotionalDescription: Hansando Island is a place where the valor of Admiral Yi Sun-sin still lives. Looking out at the sea and recalling the miracle of the Battle of Hansando, you can marvel at Admiral Yi's wisdom and courage. On this historic battlefield, you can feel the spirit of protecting the nation.

gyeongsang-020.name: Dongpirang Mural Village, Tongyeong
gyeongsang-020.summary: Tongyeong's iconic hillside mural village — where street art, ocean panoramas, and alley charm converge
gyeongsang-020.historicalDescription: Dongpirang Village was transformed through a mural project beginning in 2007. Set on a hilltop overlooking Tongyeong Port, it is characterized by murals in its narrow alleyways. It became widely known to tourists in the 2010s and is now one of Tongyeong's representative landmarks.
gyeongsang-020.emotionalDescription: Dongpirang Village is a romantic place where murals and the sea come together. Viewing the murals along the hillside alleyways and feeling the spirit of Tongyeong, and the view of Tongyeong Port from above the village is a truly special experience. It is where art and nature meet.

gyeongsang-021.name: Oedo Island (Ocean Garden), Geoje
gyeongsang-021.summary: A miraculous sea garden built over 30 years off Geoje — Korea's most beautiful botanical island
gyeongsang-021.historicalDescription: Oedo is a small island off Geoje, famous as a privately developed maritime garden. Over 30 years from 1969, the garden known as 'Nature World' was created and designated a National Scenic Site in 2001.
gyeongsang-021.emotionalDescription: Oedo is a miracle of a garden created upon the sea. The harmony of the dramatic rock formations of Haegumgang surrounding the island with the garden is spectacular, and the scenery viewed from the sea cruise boat is unforgettable. It is a mysterious space where the sea and garden become one.

gyeongsang-022.name: Haegumgang Coast, Geoje
gyeongsang-022.summary: Geoje's most spectacular coastal scenery — towering rock formations rising from an emerald sea
gyeongsang-022.historicalDescription: Haegumgang is a coastal area in southern Geoje, designated a National Scenic Site in 1971. The name Haegumgang derives from the legend that Geumgangsan Mountain flew here by sea. The scenery of dramatic rock formations meeting the clear sea is truly extraordinary.
gyeongsang-022.emotionalDescription: Haegumgang is a beautiful coast that rivals even the legendary Geumgangsan. Marveling at the harmony of the imposing rock formations and the emerald sea, and viewing the coastal scenery from a cruise boat, you feel the awesome power of nature in full.

gyeongsang-023.name: Jinjuseong Fortress, Jinju
gyeongsang-023.summary: Symbol of the Imjin War — the fortress of patriot General Kim Si-min and the heroine Nongae
gyeongsang-023.historicalDescription: Jinjuseong Fortress is the site where General Kim Si-min and Nongae gave their lives during the Imjin War in 1592. Designated a Historic Site in 1963, it features Chokseongnu Pavilion, Bukjangdae Platform, and General Kim Si-min's Martyrdom Stele. The Jinju Namgang Lantern Festival is held here annually.
gyeongsang-023.emotionalDescription: Jinjuseong Fortress is a place where the spirit of the Imjin War still lives. Gazing at the Namgang River from Chokseongnu Pavilion and feeling the patriotism of General Kim Si-min and Nongae, and walking along the fortress walls to experience the weight of history — the fantastic atmosphere of the lantern festival is a special experience.

gyeongsang-024.name: Jinju Namgang Lantern Festival
gyeongsang-024.summary: One of Korea's top 3 festivals — thousands of illuminated lanterns floating magically on the Namgang River
gyeongsang-024.historicalDescription: The Jinju Namgang Lantern Festival has been held since 2000, originating from the custom of floating lanterns to celebrate victory during the Imjin War. Held every October, it presents the spectacular sight of countless lanterns floating on the Namgang River.
gyeongsang-024.emotionalDescription: The Namgang Lantern Festival is a starlight festival on the Namgang River. The Namgang River lit with thousands of lanterns creates a fantastical scene, and the festival where history and culture coexist becomes an unforgettable memory.

gyeongsang-025.name: Eoreumgol (Ice Valley), Miryang
gyeongsang-025.summary: A mysterious valley that produces ice even in the heat of summer — a nationally designated Natural Monument
gyeongsang-025.historicalDescription: Eoreumgol was designated Natural Monument No. 224 in 1964. Even in summer, cold air emanates and ice forms in this mysterious valley — a scientifically fascinating natural phenomenon unique to this location.
gyeongsang-025.emotionalDescription: Eoreumgol is a mysterious space created by nature. On a hot summer day, experiencing the cool breeze and touching real ice here, you marvel at the wonder of nature. It is Miryang's hidden natural treasure and a perfect summer retreat.

jeju-001.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak), Jeju
jeju-001.summary: A UNESCO World Natural Heritage volcanic crater — Jeju's most iconic and dramatic sunrise destination
jeju-001.historicalDescription: Seongsan Ilchulbong is a volcanic formation created approximately 5,000 years ago by an underwater eruption. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2007. The 182m crater is a natural monument, and the sunrise from the summit is spectacular.
jeju-001.emotionalDescription: Seongsan Ilchulbong symbolizes the mysterious birth of Jeju. Climbing the crater and marveling at the awesome power of nature, the sunrise welcomed from the summit brings new hope and wonder. It is an essential stop on any Jeju trip and the place that presents the most beautiful memories.

jeju-002.name: Udo Island, Jeju
jeju-002.summary: The 'Bull Island' — Jeju's most charming satellite island, perfect for cycling and coastal discovery
jeju-002.historicalDescription: Udo is an island in front of Seongsan Ilchulbong, named Udo (牛島, Bull Island) because it resembles a lying cow. It is an island where agricultural and fishing cultures coexist, and has recently developed greatly as a tourist destination.
jeju-002.emotionalDescription: Udo is a jewel-like island of Jeju. Riding an electric cart or bicycle around the island while admiring the silver grass fields, white sandy beaches, and rocky coastline, you can feel Jeju's diverse charms. Peanut ice cream and hallabong citrus are Udo's beloved local specialties.

jeju-003.name: Manjanggul Lava Tube, Jeju
jeju-003.summary: One of the world's longest lava tubes — a UNESCO World Natural Heritage underground wonder
jeju-003.historicalDescription: Manjanggul Lava Tube was formed approximately 300,000 years ago. Of its total 7.4km length, 1km is open to the public. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2007 and preserves the world's largest lava column.
jeju-003.emotionalDescription: Manjanggul is a subterranean palace created by nature. Walking through the mysterious space of lava columns, stalactites, and stalagmites, you can feel the deep history of the Earth. It is a special place to experience the mystery of Jeju's volcanic island.

jeju-004.name: Hallasan Mountain, Jeju
jeju-004.summary: South Korea's highest peak and UNESCO World Natural Heritage — the spiritual heart of Jeju
jeju-004.historicalDescription: Hallasan is South Korea's highest peak at 1,947m. Designated a national park in 1970, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2007. Together with Seongsan Ilchulbong, it is a representative volcano of Jeju, and the Baengnokdam crater lake is famous.
jeju-004.emotionalDescription: Hallasan is Jeju's sacred mountain and Korea's pride. Walking the hiking trails and admiring the ever-changing seasonal scenery, the sunrise welcomed from Baengnokdam at the summit enriches life. It is an experience of being overwhelmed by the awesome majesty of nature.

jeju-005.name: Hyeopjae Beach, Jeju
jeju-005.summary: Jeju's most celebrated beach — emerald waters, white sand, and a stunning view of Biyangdo Island
jeju-005.historicalDescription: Hyeopjae Beach is a beach in Jeju City, famous for the view of Biyangdo Island in the distance. White sandy beaches and emerald sea combine harmoniously, and it was selected as one of Korea's 100 Great Tourist Destinations by the Korea Tourism Organization in 2008.
jeju-005.emotionalDescription: Hyeopjae Beach shows the very essence of Jeju's sea. Walking on the sandy beach while admiring the emerald water, and the scenery with Biyangdo as a backdrop is like stepping into a photograph. It is an essential stop on any Jeju trip.

jeju-006.name: Bijarim Forest, Jeju
jeju-006.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage torreya forest with ancient trees over 2,000 years old — a verdant sacred sanctuary
jeju-006.historicalDescription: Bijarim is a torreya (nutmeg-yew) forest, designated a natural monument in 1992. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2007 and is densely populated with torreya trees over 2,000 years old.
jeju-006.emotionalDescription: Bijarim offers the special experience of walking through a millennium-old forest. Walking among the densely growing torreya trees and feeling the mystery of the evergreen forest, you can find peace of mind in what feels like time suspended in place.

jeju-007.name: Chilsimni Park, Jeju
jeju-007.summary: A park within the Jungmun Resort Complex, featuring a Teddy Bear Museum and lush resort greenery
jeju-007.historicalDescription: Chilsimni Park is a park within the Jungmun Resort Complex, famous for the Teddy Bear Museum and its open lawns. It is adjacent to Jungmun Beach and attracts many families and tourists.
jeju-007.emotionalDescription: Chilsimni Park is a wonderful space to enjoy with family. Feeling a childlike innocence at the Teddy Bear Museum and spending a relaxed time on the lawn — it is a nice place to enjoy the leisure atmosphere of Jungmun Resort.

jeju-008.name: Marado Island, Jeju
jeju-008.summary: South Korea's southernmost inhabited island — a dramatic coastal destination known for its lighthouse and clear sea
jeju-008.historicalDescription: Marado is the southernmost inhabited island of South Korea, developed as a tourist destination since the 1980s. The entire island is designated a natural monument and the Seonginbong lighthouse is famous.
jeju-008.emotionalDescription: Marado offers a special experience at the very southernmost tip of South Korea. Marveling at the harmony of the blue sea and white lighthouse, the spectacular scenery surrounding the island becomes an unforgettable memory. The sense of liberation felt at land's end is uniquely captivating.

chungcheong-020.name: Daecheon Beach, Boryeong
chungcheong-020.summary: The largest beach in Chungcheong — famous for its annual Boryeong Mud Festival
chungcheong-020.historicalDescription: Daecheon Beach has been in use since the 1930s and is the largest beach in Chungcheong Province. The Boryeong Mud Festival has been held here annually since 1998, drawing nationwide visitors.
chungcheong-020.emotionalDescription: Daecheon Beach is a place filled with the joy of the Mud Festival. You can have a fantastic time playing in the mud and enjoy summer on the wide sandy beach.

chungcheong-021.name: Sapgyocheon Stream, Dangjin
chungcheong-021.summary: Dangjin's signature stream — restored as an ecological waterway with weeping willows and walking paths
chungcheong-021.historicalDescription: Sapgyocheon is a stream running through Dangjin that was recently restored as an ecological waterway. It is now a popular rest area for residents, featuring weeping willows and well-maintained walking paths.
chungcheong-021.emotionalDescription: Sapgyocheon is a place to enjoy Dangjin's natural scenery. Walking between the willow groves and admiring the river landscape offers a leisurely and refreshing experience.

chungcheong-022.name: Oeam Folk Village, Asan
chungcheong-022.summary: A 500-year-old traditional village with preserved hanok — folk experiences and traditional overnight stays
chungcheong-022.historicalDescription: Oeam Folk Village is a traditional village with a 500-year history. Over 60 hanok buildings are preserved, offering folk experience programs and traditional hanok accommodation.
chungcheong-022.emotionalDescription: Oeam Folk Village is a place to experience traditional Korean culture. Spending a night in a hanok, living traditional daily life, and learning about ancient customs through folk activities is deeply enriching.

gangwon-021.name: Daepo Port, Sokcho
gangwon-021.summary: Sokcho's signature fishing port — famous for its raw fish centers and fresh East Sea seafood
gangwon-021.historicalDescription: Daepo Port is Sokcho's representative fishing harbor, where diverse seafood converges. It is home to raw fish centers and a fish market, attracting large numbers of tourists.
gangwon-021.emotionalDescription: Daepo Port is the place to enjoy fresh East Sea seafood. Tasting fresh raw fish at the fish center and soaking in the lively atmosphere of the harbor is an invigorating experience.

gangwon-022.name: Taebaeksan Mountain
gangwon-022.summary: The heart of the Taebaek Mountain Range — a famous peak standing alongside Hwangji Pond
gangwon-022.historicalDescription: Taebaeksan stands at 1,567m at the center of the Taebaek Mountain Range. Elevated to national park status in 2016, it is well known for Hwangji Pond and the alpine botanical garden.
gangwon-022.emotionalDescription: Taebaeksan is the mountain that represents Taebaek's natural splendor. Enjoying the beautiful scenery of Hwangji Pond while hiking, and the panoramic view from the summit, is truly magnificent.

gangwon-023.name: Chiaksan Mountain, Wonju
gangwon-023.summary: Wonju's guardian mountain — home to Guryongsa Temple and Chiaksan National Park
gangwon-023.historicalDescription: Chiaksan stands at 1,286m as the guardian mountain of Wonju. Designated a national park in 1984, it is famous for Guryongsa Temple and Chiaksan Fortress.
gangwon-023.emotionalDescription: Chiaksan is both a resting place and a sacred mountain for Wonju's residents. Visiting Guryongsa Temple and feeling the exhilaration of reaching the summit along the hiking trail leaves an unforgettable impression.

gangwon-024.name: Sutasa Temple, Hongcheon
gangwon-024.summary: Hongcheon's beloved ancient temple — 1,400 years of history nestled in beautiful natural surroundings
gangwon-024.historicalDescription: Sutasa Temple was founded during the reign of King Jinheung of Silla, giving it a 1,400-year history. Situated amid Hongcheon's beautiful natural scenery, it draws many visitors throughout the year.
gangwon-024.emotionalDescription: Sutasa is a tranquil temple nestled in the natural beauty of Hongcheon. Meditating and healing amid the beautiful scenery surrounding the temple offers a deeply peaceful and restorative experience.

gangwon-025.name: Soyang River Skywalk, Chuncheon
gangwon-025.summary: A thrilling glass-floored observation deck over the Soyang River — Chuncheon's defining new landmark
gangwon-025.historicalDescription: The Soyang River Skywalk opened in 2016 as a glass-floored observation deck projecting out over the Soyang River. It offers a breathtaking experience and has become a new landmark of Chuncheon.
gangwon-025.emotionalDescription: The Soyang River Skywalk offers a truly thrilling experience. The vertiginous sensation and sweeping views when looking down at the Soyang River through the glass floor create memories that can never be forgotten.

gyeonggi-024.name: Pyeongtaek Port
gyeonggi-024.summary: A large West Sea fishing port — charming harbor scenery and abundant fresh seafood
gyeonggi-024.historicalDescription: Pyeongtaek Port is a large West Sea fishing port where diverse seafood converges. The harbor scenery and fishing village atmosphere are attractive, and the nearby Pyeongtaek-Songtan area adds cultural depth.
gyeonggi-024.emotionalDescription: Pyeongtaek Port is a place to feel the ambiance of a West Sea fishing village. Walking along the harbor, browsing fresh seafood, and enjoying the unhurried atmosphere of the fishing community offers a relaxed getaway.

gyeonggi-025.name: Gwangmyeong Cave
gyeonggi-025.summary: A former gold mine transformed into a cultural complex — the metropolitan area's leading cave attraction
gyeonggi-025.historicalDescription: Gwangmyeong Cave was used as a gold mine from 1912 to 1972. Converted into a cultural complex in 2011, it is the only cave tourist attraction in the Seoul metropolitan area and draws large crowds.
gyeonggi-025.emotionalDescription: Gwangmyeong Cave is a successful example of industrial heritage transformed into a cultural space. Enjoying the fantastic lighting displays and live performances inside the cave is a uniquely special experience.

gyeonggi-026.name: Gimpo Hangang New Town
gyeonggi-026.summary: A newly developed city along the Han River — popular for its waterfront parks and riverside scenery
gyeonggi-026.historicalDescription: Gimpo Hangang New Town is a new urban development from the 2000s. Created alongside Han River waterfront parks, it achieves a harmonious balance between nature and city living.
gyeonggi-026.emotionalDescription: Gimpo Hangang New Town is a relaxed city set against the backdrop of the Han River. Walking along the waterfront parks while enjoying river views and feeling the vitality of a new city is refreshing and invigorating.

gyeongsang-026.name: Ganjeolgot Cape, Ulsan
gyeongsang-026.summary: The first place in Korea to see the sunrise — a beloved dawn destination greeting the new year
gyeongsang-026.historicalDescription: Ganjeolgot is the easternmost point on the Korean Peninsula, where the sun rises earliest in all of Korea. Designated a national scenic site in 1997, it hosts an annual sunrise ceremony each New Year's Day.
gyeongsang-026.emotionalDescription: Ganjeolgot is where the very first rays of the New Year's sun appear over Korea. The sunrise witnessed from the tip of the land fills visitors with hope and profound emotion.

gyeongsang-027.name: Daewangam Park, Ulsan
gyeongsang-027.summary: Ulsan's signature coastal park — famous for its dramatic rock formations and historic lighthouse
gyeongsang-027.historicalDescription: Daewangam Park was developed in 1986 as a coastal park near Ganjeolgot. It is famous for the Daewangam rock formation and its lighthouse. Rock carvings inscribed on the boulders are also a notable highlight.
gyeongsang-027.emotionalDescription: Daewangam Park showcases the majestic scenery of the East Sea coast. Walking along the coastal cliffs and feeling the grandeur of the ocean, the sunrise view here is truly spectacular.

gyeongsang-028.name: Homigot Cape, Pohang
gyeongsang-028.summary: The easternmost tip of the Korean Peninsula — home to the New Millennium Memorial Hall and famous for its sunrise
gyeongsang-028.historicalDescription: Homigot is the farthest eastward-projecting point on the Korean Peninsula, where the New Millennium Memorial Hall stands. Developed to greet the new millennium in 1999, it hosts a beloved annual sunrise ceremony.
gyeongsang-028.emotionalDescription: Homigot symbolizes new beginnings. The sunrise as seen from the New Millennium Memorial Hall inspires hope, and the sense of liberation felt at the very tip of the Korean Peninsula is uniquely profound.

gyeongsang-029.name: Donggung-won, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-029.summary: A combined zoo and botanical garden — a beloved family outing destination in Gyeongju
gyeongsang-029.historicalDescription: Donggung-won is a zoo in Gyeongju that opened in 1973. Featuring a variety of animals and plants, it is particularly popular with families visiting the historic city.
gyeongsang-029.emotionalDescription: Donggung-won is a place to enjoy nature and animals with family. Observing diverse wildlife and reflecting on the value of life, then spending a relaxed afternoon in the spacious park, is a genuinely rewarding experience.

gyeongsang-030.name: Bomun Tourism Complex, Gyeongju
gyeongsang-030.summary: Gyeongju's premier tourism complex — a resort destination centered on Bomun Lake with hotels and leisure facilities
gyeongsang-030.historicalDescription: Bomun Tourism Complex was developed in 1979 as Gyeongju's leading tourist resort. Centered on Bomun Lake, it features hotels, golf courses, and amusement facilities serving visitors from across Korea.
gyeongsang-030.emotionalDescription: Bomun Tourism Complex is a place to enjoy a full leisure retreat in Gyeongju. Strolling along Bomun Lake while admiring the natural scenery and relaxing comfortably at a lakeside hotel makes for a wonderful getaway.

jeju-009.name: Sanbangsan Mountain, Jeju
jeju-009.summary: A seaside volcanic peak with the Sanbang Cave Temple — connected to the dramatic Yongmeori Coast
jeju-009.historicalDescription: Sanbangsan rises 395m as a uniquely shaped volcano housing Sanbang Cave Temple on its face. Connected to Yongmeori Coast, it displays a distinctive volcanic landscape where an ancient temple and the open sea coexist.
jeju-009.emotionalDescription: Sanbangsan is a mystical place where mountain and sea meet. The ocean panorama viewed from Sanbang Cave Temple is breathtaking, and the strange rock formations of Yongmeori Coast convey nature's awesome power. Jeju's diverse terrain can all be taken in from one extraordinary vantage point.

jeju-010.name: Yongmeori Coast, Jeju
jeju-010.summary: A dramatic coastal trail below Sanbangsan — featuring dragon-head rock formations and stunning sunset views
jeju-010.historicalDescription: Yongmeori Coast is located at the foot of Sanbangsan, characterized by rock formations resembling a dragon's head. A coastal walking path has been laid out along the shore, and it is renowned both as a tourist destination and a celebrated sunset viewpoint.
jeju-010.emotionalDescription: Yongmeori Coast reveals the primal beauty of Jeju's sea. Walking along the shore as waves crash against the rocks and feeling the raw power of nature is exhilarating. At sunset, the harmony of the reddening sea and towering rock formations is truly spectacular.

jeju-011.name: Jungmun Saekdal Beach, Jeju
jeju-011.summary: Jeju's premier beach — striking cobalt-blue waters and a sweeping sandy shore within the Jungmun complex
jeju-011.historicalDescription: Jungmun Saekdal Beach has been a representative Jeju beach since the 1960s. The cobalt-blue sea and white sand create a harmonious scene, and the beach is integrated with the nearby Jungmun Tourism Complex.
jeju-011.emotionalDescription: Jungmun Saekdal Beach shows the very essence of Jeju's ocean. Enjoying summer on the cobalt-blue sea and sandy shore, you can fully savor the romance of Jeju.

jeju-012.name: Cheonjeyeon Falls, Jeju
jeju-012.summary: Jeju's iconic three-tiered waterfall — set within the Jungmun Tourism Complex
jeju-012.historicalDescription: Cheonjeyeon Falls is located within the Jungmun Tourism Complex, and Jeju legend holds that divine beings once bathed in its sacred waters. The three-tiered waterfall cascading through a lush valley is a magnificent sight.
jeju-012.emotionalDescription: Cheonjeyeon Falls reveals the beauty of Jeju's natural world. Strolling through the valley to the sound of the waterfall, the clear water and surrounding greenery purify the mind and restore the spirit.

jeju-013.name: Seopjikoji, Jeju
jeju-013.summary: A scenic cape near Seongsan Ilchulbong — celebrated as a beloved drama filming location
jeju-013.historicalDescription: Seopjikoji is a coastal area near Seongsan Ilchulbong; 'Seopji' is a Jeju dialect word meaning 'narrow land.' After becoming famous as a drama filming location, it grew into one of Jeju's most popular tourist destinations.
jeju-013.emotionalDescription: Seopjikoji showcases the beauty of Jeju's eastern coast. Walking along the shore and admiring the blue sea alongside Seongsan Ilchulbong in the distance brings out the full romance of Jeju.

jeju-014.name: Gimnyeong Beach, Jeju
jeju-014.summary: An east-coast beach with enchanting emerald waters — a rising star on social media
jeju-014.historicalDescription: Gimnyeong Beach is located on Jeju's eastern coast, characterized by emerald waters and fine white sand. Its natural beauty has recently gained widespread popularity through social media.
jeju-014.emotionalDescription: Gimnyeong Beach reveals the beauty of Jeju's eastern sea. Spending leisurely time in the emerald water and white sand, you can easily fall under the spell of Jeju's natural charm.

jeju-015.name: Geumneung Beach, Jeju
jeju-015.summary: A quiet western beach known for its distinctive dark sand and emerald sea
jeju-015.historicalDescription: Geumneung Beach is located on Jeju's west coast, distinctive for its dark volcanic sand. Adjacent to Hyeopjae Beach, it is beloved for its peaceful and unhurried atmosphere.
jeju-015.emotionalDescription: Geumneung Beach is a place to enjoy Jeju's sea in peaceful solitude. Admiring the striking contrast of dark sand and emerald water, you can enjoy a quiet, deeply restful retreat.

jeju-016.name: Osulloc, Jeju
jeju-016.summary: Jeju's green tea museum and theme park — an immersive green tea culture experience
jeju-016.historicalDescription: Osulloc is a green tea theme park that opened in 2001. Operated by AmorePacific, it features expansive tea fields, a museum, and a café beloved by visitors from across Korea.
jeju-016.emotionalDescription: Osulloc is a place to experience Jeju's distinctive green tea culture. Walking through the tea fields and learning about tea culture, then savoring green tea desserts, makes for a relaxed and genuinely enriching afternoon.

jeju-017.name: Saryeoni Forest Path, Jeju
jeju-017.summary: A pristine forest trail along Bijarimno Road — the very essence of Jeju's woodland beauty
jeju-017.historicalDescription: Saryeoni Forest Path is a woodland trail along Bijarimno Road that opened in 2009. The beautiful trail integrated with Saryeoni Oreum is beloved as one of Jeju's premier walking destinations.
jeju-017.emotionalDescription: Saryeoni Forest Path is a place to feel the beauty of Jeju's forests. Walking along Bijarimno Road and immersing yourself in Jeju's pristine nature, the peaceful forest ambiance provides profound healing and restoration.

jeju-018.name: Aqua Planet Jeju
jeju-018.summary: Jeju's premier aquarium — home to a diverse array of marine life and popular live shows
jeju-018.historicalDescription: Aqua Planet Jeju opened in 2012 as a large-scale aquarium. It showcases a diverse range of marine life, and its live performances and hands-on programs are consistently popular with visitors.
jeju-018.emotionalDescription: Aqua Planet is a place to discover the wonders of marine life. Observing diverse creatures and learning about ocean ecosystems, then engaging with marine animals through live shows, creates a memorable and meaningful experience.

jeolla-026.name: Asia Culture Center, Gwangju
jeolla-026.summary: The hub of Asian culture in Korea — a landmark modern cultural complex in the heart of Gwangju
jeolla-026.historicalDescription: The Asia Culture Center opened in 2015 as a large cultural complex. Designated as the ACC (Asian Culture Center) in 2012, it serves as a central hub for cultural exchange across Asia.
jeolla-026.emotionalDescription: The Asia Culture Center is a space to experience the full breadth of Asian culture. Diverse exhibitions and performances offer direct and inspiring encounters with the richness of cultures from across the Asian continent.

jeolla-027.name: Suncheon National Garden
jeolla-027.summary: A sprawling national garden adjacent to Suncheonman Bay — featuring 23 diverse themed garden sections
jeolla-027.historicalDescription: Suncheon National Garden opened in 2013 as a large-scale garden attraction. With 23 themed gardens, it is closely integrated with Suncheonman Bay as a key tourist destination in South Jeolla.
jeolla-027.emotionalDescription: Suncheon National Garden showcases the beauty of diverse garden styles from around the world. Walking through thematically arranged gardens and admiring the flowers and trees across all four seasons is a truly uplifting experience.

jeolla-028.name: Boseong Green Tea Fields
jeolla-028.summary: Korea's premier green tea growing region — a breathtaking landscape of rolling tea plantations
jeolla-028.historicalDescription: Boseong is Korea's leading green tea production area, with cultivation beginning in the 1930s. The Daehan Dawon tea fields became famous as a drama filming location and subsequently grew into a major tourist attraction.
jeolla-028.emotionalDescription: Boseong's green tea fields offer a magnificent panorama of lush, rolling tea plants. Strolling through the vast tea plantations and breathing in the fresh fragrance of tea, then pausing to enjoy a quiet cup, is a serene and restorative experience.

jeolla-029.name: Ttangkkeut Village, Haenam
jeolla-029.summary: The southernmost tip of the Korean mainland — a deeply symbolic destination at the very end of the peninsula
jeolla-029.historicalDescription: Ttangkkeut Village is situated at the southernmost point of the Korean mainland. Developed as a tourist destination in 1987, it features the Ttangkkeut Monument and a sculpture park commemorating the land's end.
jeolla-029.emotionalDescription: Ttangkkeut Village offers a profoundly moving experience at Korea's southernmost edge. Standing at the Ttangkkeut Monument, gazing out at the open sea, and sensing the full breadth of the Korean Peninsula is an experience unlike any other.

jeolla-030.name: Cheongsando Island, Wando
jeolla-030.summary: A Slow City certified island — the very embodiment of slow travel in Korea
jeolla-030.historicalDescription: Cheongsando became Korea's first island to join the international Slow City network in 2011. It is a destination that pursues the values of slow living, with tradition and nature beautifully preserved throughout.
jeolla-030.emotionalDescription: Cheongsando shows the essence of slow travel. Walking the Cheongsando Slow Trail and immersing yourself in the island's unhurried pace, then discovering the value of life amid its preserved tradition and unspoiled nature, is a deeply meaningful journey.

jeolla-031.name: Namsan Mountain, Suncheon
jeolla-031.summary: Suncheon's central mountain — offering sweeping views of Suncheonman Bay and the surrounding city
jeolla-031.historicalDescription: Namsan is a mountain located in the heart of Suncheon city. Its scenery, beautifully complemented by Suncheonman Bay, is well-loved by locals and visitors alike, and the mountain's hiking and walking trails are well developed.
jeolla-031.emotionalDescription: Namsan in Suncheon is a place to take in the natural beauty of Suncheon all at once. The panorama of Suncheonman Bay seen from the summit is magnificent, and it offers a wonderful opportunity to enjoy nature within the very heart of the city.

seoul-031.name: Lotte World Tower
seoul-031.summary: South Korea's tallest skyscraper — Seoul's defining modern landmark towering over the city
seoul-031.historicalDescription: Lotte World Tower is a 123-story, 555m skyscraper completed in 2017. Upon completion it was the fifth-tallest building in the world, and it has since become an iconic structure that transformed Seoul's skyline.
seoul-031.emotionalDescription: Lotte World Tower symbolizes the present and future of Seoul. The sweeping panorama of Seoul from the observation deck is majestic, and the city lights at night are nothing short of fantastic — a breathtaking showcase of modern architecture's technology and aesthetics.

seoul-032.name: Bongeunsa Temple
seoul-032.summary: Gangnam's iconic urban temple — a 1,200-year-old sanctuary nestled beside COEX
seoul-032.historicalDescription: Bongeunsa Temple was founded by National Monk Yeonhoe in 794, giving it a 1,200-year history. Relocated to its current site in 1900, it stands as a rare urban temple in the heart of Gangnam.
seoul-032.emotionalDescription: Bongeunsa is a tranquil sanctuary in the heart of the city. Experiencing the atmosphere of a traditional temple amid towering high-rise buildings, and finding meditation and rest within, is a peaceful and restorative escape. It contrasts beautifully with the vibrant energy of Gangnam surroundings.

seoul-033.name: Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs
seoul-033.summary: Joseon royal tombs in the heart of Gangnam — a UNESCO World Heritage Site amid the urban landscape
seoul-033.historicalDescription: Seonjeongneung are the tombs of Joseon King Jungjong and his queens, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the Joseon Royal Tombs in 2009. The site was fully opened to the public in 2020.
seoul-033.emotionalDescription: Seonjeongneung showcases the beauty of Joseon royal tombs in an urban setting. Walking along the shaded trails and feeling the weight of Joseon history, framed by surrounding Gangnam high-rises, offers a striking juxtaposition of past and present.

seoul-034.name: Jeongneung Royal Tomb
seoul-034.summary: The tomb of Joseon's founding king Taejo — the very beginning of the Joseon royal tomb tradition
seoul-034.historicalDescription: Jeongneung is the tomb of King Taejo Yi Seonggye, the first of the Joseon Royal Tombs to be constructed. Originally located in present-day Gaeseong, it was relocated to Seoul in 1392. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009.
seoul-034.emotionalDescription: Jeongneung symbolizes the beginning of Joseon's 500-year history. Paying respects at Taejo's tomb and reflecting on the founding of Joseon, while strolling through the beautiful grounds, one feels the full weight and grandeur of history.

seoul-035.name: Jongmyo Shrine
seoul-035.summary: The royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon Dynasty — a UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece of ritual architecture
seoul-035.historicalDescription: Jongmyo Shrine is the royal ancestral hall of the Joseon Dynasty, enshrining the spirit tablets of 19 Joseon kings. Founded by King Taejo in 1394, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage List in 1995. The Jeongjeon and Yeongnyeongjeon halls are especially renowned.
seoul-035.emotionalDescription: Jongmyo Shrine is a solemn space symbolizing 500 years of the Joseon Dynasty. Watching the Jongmyo Jerye Ritual Music ceremony and feeling the majesty of royal tradition, then standing in awe before the grand architecture of the Jeongjeon hall, is profoundly moving. It is a supreme treasure house of Korean traditional culture.

seoul-036.name: Taereung and Gangneung Royal Tombs
seoul-036.summary: A cluster of Joseon royal tombs — a cherished destination for walking through history in the city
seoul-036.historicalDescription: Taereung and Gangneung comprise a cluster of royal tombs for Joseon kings and queens. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2009, the site is located in the Taereunggol area and is well known for its scenic walking trails.
seoul-036.emotionalDescription: Taereung and Gangneung showcase the beauty of royal tombs within an urban environment. Walking the trails and feeling the history of the Joseon royal family while enjoying the changing seasonal nature is a truly rewarding experience. Here, history and nature can be experienced simultaneously in the heart of the city.

seoul-037.name: Hongneung Arboretum
seoul-037.summary: Korea's first arboretum — a historic green sanctuary with diverse plant collections in the city
seoul-037.historicalDescription: Hongneung Arboretum is Korea's first arboretum, established during the Japanese colonial period in 1922. Opened to the public in 2009, it preserves a diverse collection of plants alongside historic buildings.
seoul-037.emotionalDescription: Hongneung Arboretum is a place that traces the history of Korean arboriculture. Admiring diverse plants and learning about nature, while sensing the traces of the modern era through preserved historic buildings, makes for a rewarding urban escape.

seoul-038.name: Yeonnam-dong
seoul-038.summary: A vibrant neighborhood where youth culture and art collide — one of Seoul's most beloved hotspots
seoul-038.historicalDescription: Yeonnam-dong is a neighborhood near Hongdae that transformed into a cultural arts hub in the 2010s as young artists and writers began gathering there. It is distinctive for its unique cafés, shops, and mural-lined alleyways.
seoul-038.emotionalDescription: Yeonnam-dong is a place to feel the youthful energy of Seoul. Browsing eclectic shops and breathing in the scent of art, then strolling through the alleys and experiencing Seoul's newest cultural scene, is endlessly engaging and inspiring.

seoul-039.name: Seongbuk-dong
seoul-039.summary: Seoul's Beverly Hills — upscale residences, elegant hanok architecture, and an emerging cultural scene
seoul-039.historicalDescription: Seongbuk-dong has been known as an upscale residential neighborhood since the 1970s and 1980s. It features a distinctive blend of hanok and Western-style buildings, and more recently, cafés and galleries have moved in, transforming it into a cultural hub.
seoul-039.emotionalDescription: Seongbuk-dong is a place to experience Seoul's sophisticated atmosphere. Walking through the harmonious blend of hanok and Western architecture, enjoying refined culture, and spending a leisurely time at a café is a genuinely pleasant experience.

seoul-040.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village
seoul-040.summary: A freshly revitalized hanok street where tradition and contemporary culture coexist in perfect harmony
seoul-040.historicalDescription: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village is a newly revitalized hanok street that came to life in the 2010s. Young craftspeople and designers moved in, blending modern sensibility into the traditional hanok structures.
seoul-040.emotionalDescription: Ikseon-dong is a place where tradition and modernity come together in harmony. Exploring trendy cafés and boutiques operating inside hanok buildings, you can experience Seoul's new take on hanok culture — the charming appeal of old architecture infused with a fresh contemporary spirit.

seoul-041.name: Samcheong-dong
seoul-041.summary: An artist's street of galleries and cafés — a cultural promenade blending beauty, tradition, and creativity
seoul-041.historicalDescription: Samcheong-dong evolved into a cultural street from the 1970s as artists began gathering there. It creates a distinctive and charming ambiance through a harmonious mix of galleries, cafés, and hanok all in one place.
seoul-041.emotionalDescription: Samcheong-dong is a place where art and tradition coexist. Visiting galleries and enjoying leisure at a café, then feeling the harmony of Korean tradition and modernity in close proximity to Bukchon, is a deeply satisfying cultural experience.

seoul-042.name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
seoul-042.summary: A former railway track transformed into a linear urban park — running through Yeonnam-dong and Hongdae
seoul-042.historicalDescription: Gyeongui Line Forest Park was created by restoring the old Gyeongui Line railway that had been disused since the 2000s. Opened in 2016, it is a walking path running through Yeonnam-dong and the Hongdae neighborhood.
seoul-042.emotionalDescription: Gyeongui Line Forest Park is a green corridor in the heart of the city. Walking through the park laid along the old railway and experiencing the coexistence of city and nature is a uniquely refreshing and restorative feeling.

seoul-043.name: Bangi-dong Food Alley
seoul-043.summary: Seoul's iconic food street — a culinary destination for beloved Korean dishes since the 1980s
seoul-043.historicalDescription: Bangi-dong Food Alley has been a dedicated food street since the 1980s. It is a celebrated Seoul food destination for enjoying dishes such as jokbal (braised pork trotters), bossam, and dak-bokkeum-tang (spicy chicken stew).
seoul-043.emotionalDescription: Bangi-dong Food Alley is a place to experience Seoul's lively food culture. Tasting diverse dishes while soaking in Seoul's vibrant atmosphere is an enjoyable and deeply satisfying outing.

seoul-044.name: Ikseon-dong
seoul-044.summary: A trendy hotspot where traditional hanok architecture meets vibrant contemporary culture
seoul-044.historicalDescription: Ikseon-dong began attracting widespread attention in the 2010s when cafés and shops operating inside renovated hanok started gaining popularity. Its hallmark is a unique atmosphere where tradition and modernity blend seamlessly and naturally.
seoul-044.emotionalDescription: Ikseon-dong is a captivating place where old and new coexist in delightful tension. Enjoying modern culture inside traditional hanok settings, you can simultaneously feel the transformation and the enduring heritage of Seoul.

seoul-045.name: Seongsu-dong Café Street
seoul-045.summary: Seoul's trendiest café district — a cool, creative street born from repurposed industrial buildings
seoul-045.historicalDescription: Seongsu-dong Café Street took shape in the 2010s as cafés and shops began moving into converted factory and warehouse buildings. It has become the go-to place to experience the cutting edge of Seoul's trendsetting culture.
seoul-045.emotionalDescription: Seongsu-dong Café Street is a place to feel Seoul's newest cultural pulse. Visiting distinctive cafés and enjoying the trendy atmosphere, then strolling through streets brimming with youthful creative energy, is an invigorating and inspiring experience.

seoul-046.name: Seoul Museum of History
seoul-046.summary: A city museum documenting Seoul's history and culture — located on the historic site of Gyeonghuigung Palace
seoul-046.historicalDescription: The Seoul Museum of History opened in 2002 as Seoul's official municipal museum. It exhibits Seoul's history, culture, and daily life through the ages, and is situated on the site of the former Gyeonghuigung Palace.
seoul-046.emotionalDescription: The Seoul Museum of History is a place to survey 600 years of Seoul's rich history at a glance. Through diverse and thoughtfully curated exhibitions, visitors can develop a deep understanding of Seoul's transformation and growth over the centuries.

seoul-047.name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul
seoul-047.summary: Korea's largest contemporary art museum — situated in a landmark building near Gyeongbokgung Palace
seoul-047.historicalDescription: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul, opened in 2013 as Korea's largest contemporary art museum. It was created by renovating the former Capital Defense Command building, giving it a bold modern identity.
seoul-047.emotionalDescription: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art is the center of Korean contemporary art. Viewing diverse exhibitions stimulates artistic sensibility and imagination, and the architectural beauty of the building itself is an additional attraction worth experiencing.

seoul-048.name: Changsin-dong Sewing Alley
seoul-048.summary: Seoul's last remaining garment district — an industrial heritage alley gaining new life as an artistic neighborhood
seoul-048.historicalDescription: Changsin-dong Sewing Alley has been a garment manufacturing district since the 1960s and 1970s. In recent years, young artists have been moving in, gradually transforming it into a creative and artistic destination.
seoul-048.emotionalDescription: Changsin-dong Sewing Alley is a place where Seoul's industrial history and contemporary culture meet. The unique atmosphere — where traces of sewing factories blend with a modern creative sensibility — is genuinely captivating and unlike anywhere else in the city.
